The occupants were unable to contact anyone on three different radios, however they were located approximately one hour later by another helicopter working on the same fire.Update 9 Sept:It was determined that the helicopter was flown in a tight "pedal turn" manoeuvre, and at the completion of the turn, the winds were at the right relative angle to induce a slight loss of tail rotor effectiveness. This was compounded by the immediate application of full left pedal and raising the collective, resulting in 4 - 5 rotations of the aircraft before settling into the trees.

A04W0169: A Conair Convair 580, C-FHKF, operating as CRC455 was working on a fire 90 nm NE of Fort Nelson, BC. On the downwind leg of the second drop, the number 1 engine (Allison 501-D13D) Zone 2 fire bell and light activated. The engine was secured and CRC455 returned to Fort Nelson. The fire bell was activated due to a faulty detection loop.

A04W0170: A Conair Convair 580, C-FHKF, operating as TKR455 was at 4500 ASL near Kotcho Lake when the oil temperature on the number 1 engine (Allison 501-D13D) started to rise after take off. The crew manually adjusted the oil cooler door, power setting and airspeed in order to keep the oil temperature below the caution range. Unable to reduce the temperature, the engine was shut down as a precautionary measure. The oil cooler door was ground adjusted to the trail position until the arrival of a new oil cooler door actuator.

A04W0177: The Air Spray (1967) Ltd. Douglas B-26C, C-FCBK, was departing VFR from High Level, AB to Rainbow Lake, AB as flight ASB11. The temperature at the airport was 24 degrees C and the wind was from 190 degrees true at 3 knots.  During take off from runway 31, the pilot of the B-26  aborted the take off run at approximately 90 kts due to a power loss on one of the engines (Pratt & Whitney R2800-79),and released the load of fire retardant on the runway. The aircraft was unable to stop in the remaining distance and overran the threshold, coming to rest in an upright position in a drainage ditch  approximately 1200 feet beyond the threshold. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, sustained serious injuries and the aircraft was substantially damaged. A significant amount of fuel was spilled, however, there was no post impact fire.

A04P0313:  The Yellowhead Bell 206-L3 helicopter (C-GYHX) was supporting fire-management activities near Valemount, BC, and had landed on a log pad.  Shortly after touch-down, the pad broke apart but the pilot could not prevent the main rotor blades from striking a stump and the helicopter rolled over.  The pilot and passenger escaped with minor injuries and the helicopter was substantially damaged.  There was a small post-crash fire in the engine compartment which the pilot put out with a hand-held fire extinguisher.  BC Forestry Service was on site to examine the pad.

A04W0179: A cloud of white smoke was observed to be discharging from the left engine of the Air Spray (1967) Ltd. Douglas A26C, registration C-GXGY, following a fire bombing run. The engine (Pratt & Whitney-USA R-2800-79) was shut down and a single engine landing was carried out at Rainbow Lake, Alberta. Maintenance examination determined that one cylinder was cracked from spark plug hole to spark plug hole. The cylinder was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

A04P0330:  The Conair Convair 440/580 aircraft, registration C-GFHKF, operating as CRC455 took off from Price George on a fire supression mission. Soon after take-off the no. 1 engine (Allison 501D-13) oil temperature began to rise. Manual adjustment of the oil cooler door and power and airspeed adjustments could not keep the oil temperature below the caution range. The crew jettisoned the load of fire retardent, shut down the engine, and completed the QRH procedure. The aircraft returned to Prince George and landed without further incident. No emergency was declared but ERS responded.

A04P0333:  The Gemini Helicopters Bell 205A-1 helicopter, registration C-GREU, was engaged in forest fire fighting with a bucket on a long line, 15 nm NW of Castlegar. The pilot had just set the bucket in the water when he noticed that much more than normal left pedal was required to control the yaw. He reduced the power demand and the helicopter began to rotate inside the confined area. The helicopter rotated through 360 degrees at least three or four times. The pilot rolled the throttle partially off which lessened the rotation. As the helicopter descended, the pilot rolled the throttle completely off and landed. The main rotor blades struck trees as the helicopter touched down. The helicopter sustained minor damage and the pilot was uninjured. It was determined that a bearing on the tail rotor blade pitch link horn, on the pitch horn side, had failed and jammed between the ball of the bearing and the pitch horn of the blade, putting sufficient force on the pitch link to break it and causing tail rotor failure, resulting in loss of tail rotor control.

A04O0233: The Skyservice Airlines Airbus A330-300 aircraft, registration C-FRAV, operating as flight SSV700, was enroute when the crew received a Master Warning for a lavatory smoke indication. The In-charge flight attendant reported there was an odour from the lavatory but no evidence of smoke or fire. The flight crew declared an emergency and returned to Toronto where ARFF was standing by for the uneventful landing. Once on the ground, an inspection was carried out by the fire crew but there was no indication of fire on the aircraft. The aircraft was then given clearance to taxi to the gate. Maintenance is continuing to investigate the cause of the smoke alarm in the lavatory, and the operator will report with further findings when they become available.

A04P0390:  While the Cessna 182 (C-GBAS) was taxiing on the Springbank airpark, the left main landing gear leg broke at the fuselage box.  The left wing tip and horizontal stabilizer were damaged from ground contact.  The TSB Engineering Branch examined the broken gear leg to determine the mode of fracture, and found signs of corrosion fatigue at the point where the leg exits the fuselage supporting box.

A05P0065: The Conair DC-6 aircraft, C-GIBS, operating as CRC451T, was on a training flight at the Abbotsford airport. On climb out after a touch-and-go landing, when power was reduced to METO, the no. 3 engine (P & W R2800-CB3) manifold pressure and BMEP continued to drop, and the crew were unable to set the correct power. The crew shut down the engine in accordance with the checklist and feathered the propellor. No emergency was declared. The aircraft landed at Abbotsford without further event. Maintenance inspection determined that the supercharger clutches were slipping.

A05W0091: The Air Spray (1967) Ltd. Lockheed 188C, C-GZCF, was operating as ASB90 on a local training flight at Fort McMurray, AB. During the take off roll, the number 1 engine (Allison 501-D13) only indicated 1350 SHP where 3000 SHP was expected. The take off was aborted at approximately 50 kts and the aircraft returned to the ramp for inspection. Maintenance determined that the speed sense valve did not close the 5th and 10th stage bleed valves. An SDR will be filed with Transport Canada.

A05W0093: The Air Spray (1967) Ltd. Lockheed 188C (Electra), C-GZCF, was operating as ASB90 from Ft. McMurray, AB. During the landing rollout, the fire bell sounded and the flight crew completed the fire drill and shut down the engine (Allison 501-D13) by pulling the E-handle. Maintenance determined that the #1 engine swirl straightener detached causing the exhaust gases to infiltrate the engine cowl area causing some minor damage to the forward cowl. The aircraft was ferried to Red Deer, AB on three engines and the #1 engine was replaced.

A05W0095: The Buffalo Airways Ltd. Douglas C54G-DC (DC-4), C-GBNV, was conducting forest fire suppression work 50 nm west of Hay River, NT when the # 3 engine (Pratt & Whitney-USA R-2000-4) began to run rough. The fire retardant was dropped, the # 3 engine shutdown and the aircraft returned to Hay River. The aircraft was outside the previous evening when heavy rain showers went through the area. The ignition system was cleaned and dried and the magnetos retimed. The aircraft was returned to service with no recurrence of the problem.

A05Q0088: En croisière, à 2,500 pieds sur une patrouille de feu,  le moteur, un Lycoming 0-540, du Cessna R182 immatriculé C-GRUA, s'est mis à vibrer.  Quelques instants après avoir initié un retour à la base, plusieurs bruits de bris mécaniques ont été entendus et le moteur s'est arrêté brusquement.  Le pilote a tenté un démarrage mais aucune rotation complète de l'hélice n'a été possible.  L'atterrissage d'urgence s'est fait sur un chemin de bois.  Durant le roulement au sol les ailes ont été endommagées par les arbres en bordure du chemin. Le pilote n'a pas été blessé. Après l'atterrissage il a noté la présence d'huile sur le capot ainsi qu'une déformation provenant du moteur.  Le pilote a pu être évacué par hélicoptère.  L'examen du moteur a révélé que le baril du cylindre no 6 s'était fracturé.  Les segments du piston se sont cassés contre la rupture.  L'huile a été perdu, et tous les paliers du moteur ont subi des dommages suite au manque de lubrification.  Le cylindre ne comptait que 1,600 heures de service.  Le martelage des surfaces fracturé n'a pas permis de déterminer l'origine de la fracture.

operation: AIR TRANSPORT; FIRE FIGHTING / FIRE MANAGEMENT
Summary: A05C0095: The Walsten Air Beech 200, C-GQNJ, was arriving at Sioux Lookout, ON, on an IFR flight plan with no reported traffic. When entering the control zone the crew of GQNJ reported traffic, a Canadair CL215, off their starbord wing. The FSS also observed the CL215 after the report by GQNJ. The crew of GQNJ cancelled IFR and elected to overshoot to let the CL215 land first. The Province of Saskatewan Canadair CL215, G-FYXG, reported 3 miles final and landed. When querried by FSS, the crew of FYXG explained that they had been on the wrong frequency prior to 3 miles.

A05P0132: At 1532 Pacific daylight time on the 07 June 2005, a certification flight testing program was being conducted by Cascade Aerospace Inc. with a Bombardier DHC-8-402, serial number 4040,  modified for air tanker operations. The test flight curriculum included a series of increasing amplitude push-over/pull-up manoeuvres to evaluate stick-force-per-g (gravity) and to demonstrate satisfactory handling characteristics during a push-over to 0g with a water/retardant load on board. During the third and final push-over, the #1 and #2 engine low oil pressure annunciators both illuminated. The speed of both propellers then reduced by about 300 rpm and the engine torques increased proportionately (both events were uncommanded). A recovery to a normal attitude was completed during which both engine low oil pressure annunciators extinguished. The #1 propeller recovered back to the selected speed of 1020 rpm. However, the #2 propeller went into an overspeed condition and was governed at 1060 rpm by the overspeed governor. The #2 propeller was then intentionally feathered and the engine was shut down in accordance with the Aircraft Flight Manual checklist. The #2 engine was subsequently re-started, however, the propeller could not be un-feathered, so the engine was again shut down. The flight concluded at the departure point of Abbotsford with one engine inoperative.UPDATED: 15 JANUARY 2007THE BOARD AUTHORIZED THE RELEASE OF THIS REPORT ON 02 AUGUST 2006.

A05W0104: The Buffalo Airways C-54, C-FIQM, was inbound to Hay River, NT (CYHY), when the crew noticed a rise in oil temperature and a loss of oil pressure in the number 2 engine (P&W R2000-7M2). The engine was shut down, and aircraft continued to CYHY. The aircraft was ferried to the maintenance base at Yellowknife, where a failed main bearing was discovered, and the engine was replaced.

A05W0108: The Air Spray (1967) Ltd. Lockheed 188C Electra, C-GHZI, was performing fire suppression work in the High Level, AB area. During a power reduction for a descent to commence aerial work, the horsepower and fuel flow increased on the #4 engine (Allison 501-D13) while the other engines remained at a reduced power state. The #4 engine RPM fluctuated and decreased to 13 000 RPM and remained low at 13 100 RPM. The engine was shutdown and the aircraft returned to High Level. The prop governor had been changed on the #4 engine prior to the flight; however, no power run was completed due to ramp congestion. Maintenance adjusted the prop governor and the aircraft was returned to service.

A05P0137: The aircraft had departed Abbotsford at 1853 Pacific daylight time, under VMC, for the sixth flight of the day, and proceeded to uncontrolled airspace about 15 nm north of Abbotsford. There were two pilots and two company flight test engineers on board. A certification flight testing program was being conducted by Cascade Aerospace Inc. with the Bombardier DHC-8-402, serial number 4040, modified for air tanker operations. At about 1930, during a rate one turn in cruise flight at 4 500 feet, the #1 engine (PW150A, serial number PCE-FA0020) shutdown without warning. The auto-feather system was dis-armed, in accordance with normal procedures and the alternate feather system was used to complete feathering of the propeller. The flight returned to Abbotsford at 1950 with one engine inoperative.  UPDATED: 15 JANUARY 2007THE BOARD AUTHORIZED THE RELEASE OF THIS REPORT ON 23 AUGUST 2006.

A05W0138: The Conair Group Douglas DC-6B, registration C-GKUG, was en route Mayo to Dawson City, Yukon when the number 2 engine (Pratt and Whitney WASP CB3) developed a large oil leak. The engine was shut down and the flight continued to Dawson City without further incident. Maintenance examination determined that the torque meter plug was leaking. The engine nose case was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

A05W0132: The Conair Group Inc. amphibious Air Tractor AT-802A, C-GAAG, was conducting fire suppression work as CRC681 in the Fort McMurray, AB area. While on approach for a wheel landing in Fort McMurray, the pilot selected gear down and received no green light for the right nose gear. The pilot conducted a missed approach and circled to trouble shoot the problem. A visual inspection both by company aircraft and ground personnel resulted in the pilot deciding to complete a wheel landing. ARFF was requested by the pilot and standing by for the landing. During touchdown the green light illuminated and the aircraft taxied to the tanker base for inspection. Maintenance determined that a sensor for the wheel down indication for the front right nose wheel was loose and out of position.

A05W0133: The Ultra Helicopters Ltd. Bell 206L-3, C-GUHB, was departing from the company base to reposition to the fire base at Manning, AB to commence fire suppression activity. During the lift off, the right skid of the helicopter contacted some full fuel drums next to the helipad resulting in a dynamic rollover to the right. The pilot was uninjured; however, the helicopter sustained substantial damage.

A05C0127: The Manitoba Government Air Services CL215 water bomber, C-GUMW, had departed Grace Lake on a fire dispatch run when at 2000 ft asl, the crew noticed that the left engine (Pratt & Whitney R-2800) began to lose power. The crew turned on the electric fuel boost pump and the engine power was restored. The crew elected to return to Grace Lake and approximately 2 minutes later the engine again lost power. The engine was secured and the aircraft landed safely. The initial engine power loss was traced to a failure of the mechanical engine driven fuel pump. The second loss of power was traced to a failure of the electric fuel boost pump. Both pumps were replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

A05O0143: C-FOEW, a Dehavilland DHC-2 MKIII amphibious float equipped aircraft, operated by the Ontario Ministry of Natural Resources (MNR), was flying from Hornepayne, Ontario to Lake Esnagi to check out reports of a recreational fire. After departure from Hornepayne airport the amphibious float wheels were not retracted and remained down during the landing on Lake Esnagi. Upon touchdown on the water surface, the aircraft overturned and came to rest upside down. The pilot and passenger (conservation officer) escaped with minor injuries. An MNR helicopter in the area rescued the pilot and passenger and flew them to Wawa.

A05O0145: C-GHUM, a Bell 205A-1 helicopter, operated by Abitibi Helicopters Inc. departed Sudbury (CYSB) to inspect for forest fires in the region. Approximately 20 nm south of CYSB the engine fire light illuminated. The pilot checked for fire and performed a precautionary landing without incident. On the ground the aircraft was inspected and there was no evidence of fire. The pilot started the helicopter and it ran without incident. Maintenance advised the pilot that the helicopter had been washed that morning and the false indication was most likely due to moisture in the fire sensing system.

A05C0141: The Wildcat Helicopters Bell 212, C-GSGT, was on a flight from Brandon, Manitoba, to Regina, Saskatchewan, with the pilot and company engineer on board. This was to be one leg of several flights being conducted as the helicopter was returning to Kelowna, British Collumbia from forest fire suppression activities in Quebec. When the helicopter was approximately 70 nm east of Regina, the number-two engine torquemeter oscillated momentarily. When the throttles were retarded, both torquemeters matched. When the throttles were advanced, the number-2 engine did not respond. The pilot advised Regina Tower that they were landing with one engine out and a successful forced landing was completed in an open field. There was no damage to the helicopter; the pilot and eingineer were not injured. Because the engine temperatures went to redline before the engine could be shut down, the company is shipping an engine (Pratt & Whitney PT6T3) to replace the errant engine. Initial reports indicated compressor damage.

A05P0203:  The Conair Firecat (C-GHPJ) was over the north end of Powell Lake when the fire warning light for the number 1 engine (Wright Cyclone 1820) illuminated.  The pilot feathered the propeller and the light extinguished after 10 seconds.  The aircraft returned to Campbell River and landed but was unable to clear the taxiway.Company maintenance found a defective fire detection loop.

A05W0180: The Conair Firecat, registration C-FOPU, had departed Whitehorse, YT for Prince George, BC. Approximately 90 miles southeast of Whitehorse, the engine (Pratt and Whitney 982C9HE2-MR5-R1820) began to backfire and run rough. The engine was shut down and the aircraft returned to Whitehorse without further incident. Maintenance examination found that the problem was a stuck valve. The engine was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

A05Q0211: The CL-600-2B19 (RJ), registered C-GMJA operated by Air Canada Jazz was parked at the gate when ramp crew noticed an APU fire. Flight crew also received fire indications in the flight deck and airport fire crew was called. Passengers were deplaned by the main cabin door. The fire was extinguished without further incident.Report from the maintenance indicated that the fire was contained in the APU (Garrett GTCP 36-150) and some components where found seized. The APU was replaced and the aircraft returned to service.

A05W0250: The Slave Air (1988) Ltd. Beech King Air B200, C-FSAT, was departing from runway 25 at the Valley View, AB airport approximately one hour before sunrise. During the final stages of the take off roll, the pilot flying noticed a large brown object off to one side followed by a thud. The flight crew rejected the take-off and the aircraft was brought to a stop with 20 feet of runway remaining. The remains of a medium sized deer were found on the runway. Damage from the impact required repairs to the left main gear doors and left propeller and the removal of the left engine for a hot section overhaul. Update 23 January 2006: TC Aerodrome Safety reported that the Vallyview airport is a registered aerodrome rather than a certified site and therefore is not required to have a bird and wildlife program. In light of the oil boom and the communities geographic local the town about six months ago commissioned at feasibility study to look at the cost/ benefit of lengthening the existing runway from 3300 -5000 feet and have the aerodrome certified. An upgrade of this magnitude would allow air tanker aircraft CL 215, Fire Cat's and Convair 580's to operate out of Vallyview and offer the town a scheduled air service.This deer strike was the first time an event such as this as ever occurred since the inception of the airport there. The town does provide runway condition reports to incoming charter flights, and maintains the runway and apron lighting as well as their surfaces.

A06Q0047: Le Canadair CL-215, immatriculé C-FTXG et exploité par le Service Aérien du Gouvernement du Québec était en approche pour un atterrissage sur la piste 30 de l'aéroport de Québec. L'équipage a rapporté avoir une indication que le train principal gauche n'était pas verrouillé. L'équipage a procédé pour l'atterrissage et le train gauche s'est affaissé pendant le roulement. L'appareil s'est déposé sur le flotteur externe gauche jusqu'à son immobilisation sur la piste. L'appareil a subi des dommages au flotteur gauche et d'autres inspections sont en cours.L'examen après l'événement a confirmé que le harnais électrique pour le contacteur de position du train verrouillé baissé (Down lock switch) s'est coincé dans l'articulation du mécanisme de verrouillage. Cette condition a empêché le mécanisme de verrouiller la jambe de train d'atterrissage et a aussi causé un cours circuit au circuit d'indication de verrouillage de train. L'organisation de maintenance des aéronefs enquête les circonstances qui ont emmené ce harnais à causer cette condition.

A06W0055: The Conair Consolidated Vultee CV580 Convair water bomber, C-FKFY, CVA448 was operating in the vicinity of Wolf Lake, AB, when the No. 2 engine sustained a power loss accompanied by a TIT spike of 1100 degrees and a zone one (exhaust area) fire warning. The crew secured the engine and proceeded to their base at Lac La Biche (CYLB). Maintenance determined that the engine (Allison 501-D13H, QEC number 77) sustained a massive turbine failure. There was no fire damage to the aircraft. The engine was removed and shipped to Kelowna Flight Craft and Conair will submit an initial report on the mode of failure.Update 27 July 2006           During an engine teardown it was determined that the turbine inlet bearing (PN 687100) failed, and caused the rotor to run of its axis. This resulted in turbine blade contact with the vanes and air seals. The extra load caused failure of the rear bearing and the rear scavenge pump.            The turbine inlet bearing exhibited evidence of extreme heat damage and skidding. The rollers were worn flate at the contact point with the inner race. The separator was intact, and the inner race was worn through to the rotor shaft at one point. The bearing was a dull, flat black colour, indicating overheating. There was no indication of pre-existing oil starvation. All damage to oil feed tubes was considered to be a result of bearing failure. Destructive testing of the front bearing oil jet did not reveal blockage of the jet.

A06P0088: The Douglas DC-6B, [C-GKUG], was in cruise flight to Whitehorse at 8,500 feet ASL, when the number four engine started backfiring. The flight crew adjusted the mixtures rich, reduced power, feathered the affected propeller, and shut down the engine. The aircraft diverted to Smithers where it landed without further event. Company maintenance examined the engine and determined that a cylinder assembly was cracked. The cylinder was replaced and the aircraft returned to service.

A06P0110:  The Martin Mars JRM3 [C-FLYL] operated for forest fire fighting by Flying Tankers Inc was returning to base when the number 3 engine (Curtis-Wright Cyclone R-3350) started backfiring.  Company maintenance determined that the induction housing was cracked.

A06P0097: The crew of a Martin Mars water bomber (C-FLYL) completed a precautionary shutdown of the #2 engine (Wright R-3350 Cyclone) during a training mission because of low oil pressure indications. The aircraft returned to base. Maintenance determined that the problem was associated with the oil pressure guage.

A06C0093: The Canadair CL215, C-FYXG, was returning from a water bombing mission when the crew noted a loss of hydraulic system pressure. They carried out the alternate gear extension procedure and made an uneventful landing on runway 36 in La Ronge. The runway was closed for approximately 20 minutes while the aircraft was towed to the hangar. A subsequent inspection revealed a leaking hydraulic valve in the center wing section. The valve was replaced and the aircraft returned to service.

A06O0151:C-GOGC, an amphibious float equipped De Havilland DHC-6/300, operated by the Ontario Ministry of Natural Resources, was conducting fire suppression activities in the vicinity of Smooth Rock Falls, Ontario. The aircraft was taking off in a south-bound direction after picking up water on the Mattagami River. Shortly after take off, during the initial climb, the aircraft collided with hydro wires spanning across the river. The wires were cut and the aircraft incurred substantial damage. The aircraft was flown to Timmins without further incident.

A06W0096: The Air Spray (1967) Ltd. Canadair CL215-1A10, C-GOFR, was conducting forest fire suppression services in the vicinity of Embarrass, AB. While lifting off the water after a scoop, the left propeller went to an over-speed condition of 3100 rpm. Initially, the rpm was controllable with the power and propeller levers and rpm's were reduced to 2800, however, the flight crew decided to feather the propeller and return to Ft. McMurray. A single-engine approach and landing were performed at Ft. McMurray. Maintenance determined that the propeller governor had failed and an SDR was submitted to Transport Canada.

A06Q0103: L'hélicoptère Bell 205A1, immatriculé C-FSMI et exploité par Heli-Inter Inc. atterrissait avec à son bord un pilote et trois travailleurs forestiers pour le combat des incendies. Le pilote revenait déposer les passagers à un endroit où il s'était posé le vol précédent.  À l'atterrissage le pilote a positionné l'appareil de manière à ce que les travailleurs accèdent au compartiment cargo. Cependant le soleil était dans son champ de vision. Il a frappé la tête d'un arbre alors qu'il était en descente pour atterrir à environ quatre pieds du sol. L'appareil s'est mis à vibrer. Le pilote a déposé les passagers et a complété son vol vers Chapleau. L'hélicoptère a subi des dommages à l'intrados des pales et au bord d'attaque du rotor  principal. Une inspection spéciale devra être effectuée avant de retourner l'appareil en service.

A06C0094: The Manitoba Government Air Services Canadair CL-215, C-GYJB, was conducting a water scooping sequence at Eagle Lake, ON. An uncommanded opening of the left hand water drop door was experienced, and the door was ripped from the airframe. The aircraft returned to Gimli, MB, without further incident.

A06P0112:  The Conair Firecat (C-GHDY) was at 1500 feet on the West Route VFR arrival to Abbotsford airport from the northwest, when it came close to a Piper Cherokee at the same altitude near the "264th Street" reporting point.  The Abbotsford tower controller issued two traffic alerts to the Firecat but the pilot did not see the Piper.  The Piper was on a different radio frequency and was not aware of the Firecat.

A06W0099: The Conair Group Inc. Douglas DC-6B, C-GHLY, was conducting forest fire suppression operations in the vicinity of Manning, AB. After dropping a load of retardant, the flight crew experienced minor yawing and a fluctuating #1 BMEP (brake mean effective pressure) gauge. The #1 engine (Pratt & Whitney-USA Wasp CB3) was feathered and the aircraft completed an uneventful three engine landing in Peace River, AB. Maintenance discovered a cracked ear on one of the cylinders. The cylinder was replaced and the aircraft returned to service.

A06W0104: The Precision Helicopters Inc. Bell 206B helicopter, registration C-GPGX, was departing the Nose Mountain forestry observation tower, Alberta in support of forest fire suppression operations. Shortly after lift-off the helicopter yawed 180 degrees to the right, descended onto a steep slope and rolled onto the left side. One passenger was fatally injuried. A second passenger sustained serious injuries; the pilot and third passenger sustained minor injuries. The helicopter was substantially damaged.

A06W0116: After a water scoop when fighting a fire, the pilot of the Air Spray (1967) Ltd. CL-215-1A10 (C-FTUU) noticed a slight flicker in the manifold pressure of the left-hand engine (Pratt & Whitney USA R2800-CA3). A following CL415 advised the crew the engine was trailing smoke. The load was jettisoned, a climb was initiated, and the crew returned to Slave Lake, AB. During the return flight a CV-580 confirmed smoke but no fire evident, and the crew closely monitored the oil temp, pressure, and quantity until they landed in Slave Lake. A cracked cylinder was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

A06P0115: The Conair Firecat, [C-FOPY], was on approach to Kamloops when the pilot received a fire warning light indication and subsequently featered the propeller and shut down the number two engine. The aircraft was landed under single engine operation without further event. Company maintenance suspects an electrical fault with the fire detection system.

A06W0106: The Remote Helicopters (NWT) Ltd. Bell 206B, serial number 600, was conducting water bucketing operations in support of forest fire suppression activities approximately 23 nm northeast of Wabasca, Alberta. At approximately 1600 mountain daylight time the helicopter contacted trees adjacent to a shoreline, and broke up before coming to rest in an inverted position. The pilot, the sole occupant, was fatally injured.

A06C0102: The Saskatchewan Northern Air Operations Canadair CL215 aircraft. C-FAFN was returning from fire suppression operations and had just picked up a rinse load from Lac La Ronge.  During climbout, when the throttles were reduced to climb power, the right BMEP gauge fluctuated. The engine (Pratt & Whitney 2800) was manually shut down and the flight returned and landed uneventfully at La Ronge.  Inspection of the engine confirmed internal damage that necessitated removal and replacement of the right engine.

A06C0114: The Canadair CL215, C-GDHN, operated by Buffalo Airways as flight TKR296, was engaged in firefighting operations in the vicinity of Big Trout Lake when the crew observed increasing oil temperature and decreasing oil pressure indications and smoke coming from the right engine (Pratt & Whitney R2800 CA3). The crew shut down the right engine, feathered the propeller, and returned to Red Lake for a single-engine landing without further incident. After landing the engine was determined to be seized. The engine was removed for repair.

A06Q0127: Deux Cessna 182 exploités par Exact Air Inc circulaient sur la voie de circulation D à l'aéroport de Baie Comeau pour un décollage dans le cadre d'une patrouille de feux de forêt. Le Cessna 182 immatriculé C-GSCD suivait le Cessna 182 immatriculé C-FSCX. Alors que l'attention du pilote de C-GSCD était portée vers le manche à vent, il n'a pas remarqué que le C-FSCX s'était immobilisé avant de prendre position sur la piste. Il n'a pu freiner à temps et les deux appareils sont entrés en collision. Le C-FSCX a subi des dommages importants à la gouverne de direction et à l'élévateur. Le C-GSCD a subi des dommages à l'hélice. Personne n'a été blessé.

A06C0119: TKR505, a Saskatchewan Government Northern Air Ops CS2F-2 Tracker, C-GEQD, was conducting fire suppression activities when, during a bombing run, the pilot noticed the left engine begin to backfire. The pilot returned Prince Albert and shut the Wright 1820 engine down en route. Maintenance personel traced the backfire to a broken push rod tube tip on the #1 cylinder exhaust valve.

A06P0146: An Airspray Lockheed L188 Electra (ASB85) departed Prince George with a load of fire retardant on board. During the cruise climb, the #2 beta caution light illuminated followed by a droop in engine rpm. The crew actioned the emergency checklist and shut down the #2 engine. ATC was advised and the retardant load was jettisoned in the designated abort area. The flight returned and landed at Prince George without further event. ARFF sevices were standing by. The incident is being investigated by company maintenance.

A06P0173: The Conair Firecat aircraft, C-FEFK, was on a local flight from Abbotsford, BC. While climbing through 2,000 feet, about 10 nm east of Mission, BC the pilot noticed the right engine (Wright 1820-82) oil temperature was high (120-130 degrees C). He reduced power to 17 inches manifold pressure and opened the oil cooler doors, but the oil temperature remained high. The pilot shut down and feathered the engine, advised ATC and returned to Abbotsford, where the aircraft landed without further difficulty. Metal was found in the oil filter; a main bearing failure is suspected.

A07P0059:  The Saskatchewan Government Convair 580 aircraft, C-GVSK, was flying in the vicinity of the HUH VOR on a local training flight from Abbotsford airport when smoke appeared in the cockpit.  The crew advised ATC, requesting an immediate return to Abbotsford, where the aircraft landed without further event.  Maintenance inspection revealed that there had been an electrical fire in the no. 1 voltage regulator.

A07P0082:  The Conair Canadair CL215 aircraft, C-GFSL, operating as CRC202T, was on a maintenance test flight over Harrison Lake. In accordance with the maintenance program, the left engine was feathered. When the crew completed the unfeathering procedure, the propellor would not come out of the full feather position. The crew completed an engine shut-down procedure for the left engine and returned to Abbotsford. No emergency was declared and AFF was not activated. Maintenance checked the feathering system and wiring but could find no faults. The propellor governor solenoid is to be changed as this is considered to be the most likely cause of the fault.

A07O0121: The Ontario Ministry of Natural Resources Canadair CL 215 6B11 aircraft, registration C-GOGH, was fire fighting in the Chapleau area when the flight crew received a #2 engine fire warning. The crew followed the QRH procedures and shut down the engine. The engine fire warning remained active and the fire bottles were discharged. The aircraft returned to Chapleau airport and landed uneventfully. Maintenance determined that the fire warning indication was a result of a faulty circuit board within the engine fire indicating system.

A07W0114: The Buffalo Airways Ltd. Douglas C54G-DC air tanker, registration C-FIQM, had departed Hay River for Fort Simpson, NT. Shortly after take-off the No. 1 engine (Pratt and Whitney-USA R2000-7M2) began to lose power. The engine was shut down and the aircraft returned to Hay River without further incident. Maintenance examination determined that the engine-driven fuel pump had failed. The fuel pump was changed and the aircraft was returned to service.

A07Q0111: The Bell 206B, registration C-GSHC, was assigned to the mapping of a forest fire 22 nm south-west of Chibougamau.  The aircraft was flown approximately 150 ft AGL, at low airspeed, in high winds reported at 11 kts gusting 18 kts. While upwind, the pilot backed up slightly to give a better view of the fire perimeter to the two passengers doing mapping. The aircraft lost tail rotor effectiveness, did several 360 degree turns before descending into the trees and severing the tailboom. A post-impact fire started but was quickly extinguished by the pilot who had already exited the aircraft. He closed the fuel valve, all electrical systems and used the fire extinguisher.  The pilot confirmed that the ELT was ON. When no position report was given to the fire dispatch at the appropriate time, a helicopter was sent to look for them. They were evacuated to the local hospital. The passengers sustained minor injuries . The pilot was not hurt.  The aircraft was destroyed.

A07W0134: An Air Spray (1967) Lockheed L188 Electra aircraft, registration C-GZCF, was in the circuit at Fort McMurray, AB when the crew noticed that the oil quantity in the number three engine (Allison 501-D13) was decreasing. The engine was shut down as a precaution and C-GZCF landed at Fort McMurray. C-GZCF was subsequently ferried to Red Deer, AB where the oil loss was attributed to a failed fitting in the turbine section.

A07P0234:  The Conair Firecat aircraft, C-GHPJ, operating as CRC571, took off from Kamloops on a fire fighting mission. Six minutes after take-off, high oil temperature and low oil pressure was noticed on the no.1 engine (Wright 1820-82). The engine was shut down and the propeller feathered. An emergency was declared, ATC advised that the aircraft was returning to Kamloops, and AFF was requested. The aircraft landed at Kamloops without further event. AFF met the aircraft. The company has decided to change the engine.

A07C0126: The Saskatchewan Government Northen Air Operations Canadair CL 215, C-FAFN, was picking up water for forest fire management operations near Wollasten Lake, SK, when the crew noted abnormal right engine indications. The crew shut down the engine (P & W R2800), diverted the flight back to base at La Ronge, SK, and landed without further incident. Maintenance found a cracked no. 2 cylinder.

A07C0131: The Government of Saskatchewan Northern Air Operations CS2F-2 Grumman Tracker, C-GEQE, was en route on fire management operations when the pilot noted hydraulic mist in the cockpit. Hydraulic pressure dropped to zero in both systems. The aircraft diverted back to Prince Albert, the gear was lowered with the emergency system and the aircraft landed safely with ERS standing by. Maintenance found a broken hydraulic flap line.

A07C0132: The Government of Saskatchewan Tanker 214, a CL-215 water bomber, was returning to Flin Flon from a fire management flight when the crew noted a right engine zone 1 fire warning and shut down the right engine (P & W R2800). The generator on the left engine then failed, causing electrical and communication failures on approach. The aircraft arrived safely back at Flin Flon. No indication of an engine fire was found. Maintenance tightened connections in the fire warning circuit and the engine was run without incident.

A07C0133: Tanker 214, A Canadair CL215 water bomber, was en route on fire management operations when the crew noted a right engine zone 1 fire warning. The crew shut down the right engine (P & W R2800), diverted the flight back to La Ronge, and landed without further incident. No indication of fire was found. This aircraft had a similar occurrence (A07C0132) on the previous day. Maintenance re-checked the fire warning circuit and found a defective ceramic elbow. The elbow was replaced and the aircraft was test-flown without incident.

A07C0136: The Saskatchewan Northern Air Operations Convair 440/580 C-GSKR, was operating with a crew of two, in the vicinity of La Ronge, Saskatchewnan. While enroute, the engine oil temperature for the right engine (Allison-D22G) began increasing. When the temperature could not be controlled manually, the crew conducted a precautionary shutdown of the engine. FSS was advised that the aircraft would be landing with one engine inoperative and ARFF was requested. The aircraft landed without incident. Subsequent testing and inspection indicated that the oil cooler door actuator had failed. The actuator was replaced.

A07P0256:  The Air Spray (1967) Lockheed L-188C aircraft, C-FLJO, operating as ASB82, was conducting fire fighting operations in the Williams Lake area.  After the last of four fire retardant drops, as the aircraft was exiting the drop area, the PF noticed that aileron control deflection was about 30 degrees out of normal to the right, to maintain level flight.  The captain, who was PF, transferred control to the F/O and went to the rear of the aircraft to visually inspect the flight controls.  He observed that the right flap was split with a six foot section in the full down position and the remainder fully retracted.  The crew declared an emergency, slowed the aircraft and completed the appropriate QRH checklist, which called for a flapless landing.  A flapless approach was flown and the aircraft landed at Williams Lake without further event.  AFF met the aircraft.  The company will change the right hand flap panel.

operation: AIR TRANSPORT; FIRE FIGHTING / FIRE MANAGEMENT
Summary: A07O0231: The Air Georgian Beechcraft 1900D, registration C-GZGA, operating as flight GGN 7371, was taking off on runway 01 when the flight crew noted a high ITT on the number one engine. The take-off was aborted and the aircraft taxied back to the ramp via Bravo taxiway. While taxiing, Kingston radio advised of a Twin Otter on base leg for runway 25. In the meantime the captain was off COMM1 and on the PA briefing the passengers. The first officer advised the captain of the Twin Otter traffic. Prior to crossing runway 25 both pilots checked both directions on runway 25 and observed no traffic. Halfway across the runway the flight crew looked to their left and saw the Twin Otter stopped on runway 25 short of their position.

A07P0357: At 1602 Pacific daylight time, the privately registered Piper PA-34-200 Seneca (registration C GHFD, serial number 34-7350210) was cleared for takeoff from Runway 08 Right at the Vancouver International Airport destined for Pitt Meadows Regional Airport. The flight was operating under visual flight rules with only the pilot on board. Shortly after takeoff, communications and radar contact were lost. The aircraft collided with a 15-storey residential building in Richmond, about 1.5 nautical miles east-southeast of the departure end of Runway 08 Right. The pilot was fatally injured. There was no post-impact fire. The aircraft entered a suite occupied by two people; one received serious non-life-threatening injuries, the other received minor injuries. Structural damage to the building was minimal, but there was extensive water damage from the fire suppression system. As a result, hundreds of people were displaced from their homes for extended periods. There were no other reported injuries. UPDATE: 23 SEPTEMBER 2009THE BOARD AUTHORIZED THE RELEASE OF THIS REPORT ON 20 AUGUST 2009.

A08W0023: The First Air Aerospatiale ATR42-300, C-FIQR was parked at the Yellowknife Braden-Burry Expediting ramp after a flight from Ekati mine, NT (CYOA). While the passengers were deplaning, the right engine (P&W 120) was running with the propeller brake engaged (H Mode). As the crew was shutting down the engine, they received a "Prop Unlock" warning light, and flames were noticed emitting from the engine. The "On Ground Engine Fire" checklist was actioned, including discharging the fire bottles. An emergency was declared on ground frequency. ARFF responded, but their services were not required, since the fire had been extinguished by the aircraft fire suppression system. There were no reported injuries or damage to the aircraft beyond that sustained by the propeller brake.

A08P0034: The pilot of the Rockwell Intl. Turbo Aero Commander AC69 aircraft, registration C-FCZZ, operated by Conair during a post-winter maintenance activation flight test, reported a frozen left engine (Garrett TPE 331-252K) throttle cable. The aircraft was overflying the Hope airport at flight level FL230, and OAT of -23 degrees Celsius. The pilot feathered the left engine propeller, and returned to Abbottsford where the aircraft landed without further event. Company maintenance inspected the aircraft engine controls and determined that water, possibly from condensation, had migrated inside the throttle cable sleeve and frozen in flight. They blew out the cable with nitrogen to clear out any remaining moisture. These cables are not lubricated. The pilot recalled experiencing similar events on two previous occasions.

A08P0069:  The Conair CV580 aircraft, C-GKFO, took off from Abbotsford for a test flight which included the shutdown and restarting of both engines.  The no. 1 engine was shut down and the propellor feathered.  After 1 minute, the crew attempted to restart the engine but were unsuccessful.  They returned to Abbotsford, where the aircraft landed without further event.  Maintenance found that the no. 1 engine propellor had decoupled. The RGB coupling is to be replaced.

A08W0093: After a water drop, the right engine (Pratt & Whitney-USA, R-2800-CA3) on the Air Spray (1967) CL215, C-FTUW, began to run rough and backfire during climb out. Maximum power was used to climb to a safe altitude, and when power was reduced on the engine, it lost all power. The engine was secured and the propeller feathered, followed by a single engine landing at the aircraft's Lac La Biche, AB (CYLB) base. Maintenance determined that the number 11 cylinder sustained a valve failure. An SDR will be submitted to Transport Canada.

A08P0138:  The Air Spray Ltd. Lockheed L-188 aircraft, C-FLJO, was engaged in fire fighting operations in the Williams Lake area.  After the first drop and when retracting the flaps to 78 % the crew noticed that a flap asymmetry light was on and the flaps were locked at nearly the 100 % down position.  The first officer went aft to check the actual flap position and observed that the right hand flap had buckled at the outboard section.  The crew completed the QRH flap asymmetry checklist and returned to Williams Lake, where the aircraft landed without further event.

A08W0094: The AFI Leasing CL215, N264V, was on a ferry flight between Prince George, BC and Whitehorse, YT. When the aircraft was 20 nm south of Teslin, YT (CYZW), the left engine (Pratt & Whitney-USA, R-2800-CA3) oil pressure began to drop and the oil temperature increased. The crew shut the engine down, and diverted to CYZW. Metal was found in the oil screens from a suspected failed bearing. The engine was changed, and a strip report will be forwarded to the TSB.

A08W0097: A Conair Convair CV580 , C-FKFM, was operating as CRC454 10 nm east of Fort McMurray, AB when the crew noted that the right engine (Allison 501-D13) had de-coupled. The engine was secured and CRC454 returned to Fort McMurray. AARF was called out as a precaution. The aircraft landed without incident. Maintenace confirmed that the engine had de-coupled and that oil was leaking from the five and dime valves. The engine was removed and replaced. An SDR (20080526003) was submitted.

A08W0105: The Conair Canadair CL215, C-GFSN, was conducting fire suppression operations east of Slave Lake, AB, when the No. 1 engine (PRATT & WHITNEY-USA, WASP CA3) began to run rough and backfire. The flight crew shut down the engine and performed an uneventful single-engine approach and landing into Slave Lake. Maintenance found that an exhaust valve on the No. 9 cylinder was missing and presumed ingested by the engine.

A08C0124: The Meadow Air Cessna 337D, C-GYHW, was returning to Buffalo Narrows, SK from Stony Rapids, after having dropped off a passenger. Approximately 14 miles NE of the airport the pilot declared an emergency due to a double engine power loss. The pilot completed a forced landing in a swampy area on the east shore of Churchill Lake. RCC dispatched a helicopter from Cold Lake. The pilot was transported to hospital in Ile-a-la-Crosse and was subsequently released with minor injuries.

A08C0132: The Province of Ontario MNR Canadair CL215T, registration C-GOGD operating as TKR270 returned from a local flight to Kenora with one engine shutdown (Pratt & Whitney PW123AF). Information provided indicated that the engine experienced a power loss and was then shut down by the crew. Subsequent maintenance action found a fuel leak.

A08P0190:  The Conair CS2F Firecat aircraft, C-GHDY, operating as CRC573, took off from Kamloops for a fire fighting mission.  After take-off the pilot noticed that the no. 1 engine (Wright 1830) oil temperature was close to maximum and climbing.  He retarded the no. 1 engine throttle, jettisoned the retardant, and shut down the engine, feathering the propellor.  He returned to Kamloops where the aircraft landed without further difficulty.  AFF was placed on stanby as a precaution.  Maintenance found metal in the engine oil screen.  The engine is to be changed.  The company will file an SDR.

A08P0200:  The Coulson Flying Tankers Martin Mars MJRM-3 aircraft, C-FLYL, took off from Sproat Lake for Lake Shasta.  En route, while engine power was being increased to climb power from cruise power, the no. 4 engine (Curtiss Wright R3350-24WA Cyclone) began to backfire and the crew noticed a substantial drop in B.M.E.P.  The crew shut down the no. 4 engine and returned to Sproat Lake, where the aircraft landed without further difficulty.  The no. 4 engine was changed.

A08P0198:  The Coulson Flying Tankers Martin Mars MJRM-3 aircraft, C-FLYL, took off from Sproat Lake for Lake Shasta.  En route the crew attempted to feather the no. 4 engine (Curtiss Wright R3350-24WA Cyclone) as part of a maintenance flight check.  A circuit breaker failed during the feathering and smoke appeared in the cockpit.  The crew shut down the affected circuit and the smoke cleared.  The feathering of the no. 4 engine was completed manually and the aircraft returned to Sproat Lake, where it landed without further event.  The circuit breaker was replaced, the prop circuits, component lines and prop motor circuits were inspected and the aircraft was returned to service.

A08P0199:  The Conair Firecat aircraft, C-GHPJ, took off from Kamloops for a fire fighting mission.  During the climb through 5,000 feet the no. 1 engine (Wright 1820-82) fire warning illuminated.  The pilot retarded the left throttle but the fire warning remained.  He completed the feathering procedure for the left engine and the fire warning went out.  The pilot could see no indication of fire or smoke.

A08W0129: The Conair Douglas DC-6B aircraft, registration C-GKUG, was south of Dawson City, YT when it was noticed that the indication on the #4 brake mean effective pressure gauge had dropped to zero. The #4 oil quantity gauge then revealed an oil quantity loss  from 25 gallons to 12 gallons in a few minutes. It was decided to feather the prop on the #4 engine (Pratt & Whitney Wasp CB3). An uneventful landing was carried out at Dawson City. The company has indicated that the probable cause is a scavenge oil pump failure.

A08C0146: The Saskatchewan Government Canadair CL215, C-FAFN, had completed a maintenance test flight and was manouvering on the airport ramp in Stony Rapids, SK, when its right wingtip float struck a fence post on the airport ramp's perimeter chain link fence. The wing float was replaced with a spare, and the aircraft was returned to service.

A08C0166: The Boeing 747-400 freighter, operated by Cathay Pacific Airways as flight CPA092, was cruising en route when the crew received a forward cargo fire warning indication. The crew carried out emergency procedures which included activating on board fire suppression systems, declared an emergency, and diverted the flight to Winnipeg. During the diversion the fire warning terminated and the flight landed on runway 18 without further incident. After landing, the aircraft was stopped on runway 13 for inspection by ARFF staff who determined the fire warning had been false.

A08P0245:  The Conair Firecat aircraft, C-FEFK, operating as CRC574, took off from Penticton for a ferry flight to Abbotsford.  When approaching Abbotsford airport, the left engine (Curtiss Wright R1820) began rapid backfiring.  Although all engine gauges were normal, the pilot secured the engine and feathered the propellor in accordance with the QRH checklist.  The aircraft landed at Abbotsford without further difficulty. Maintenance found the #9 cylinder exhaust rocker bolt sheered at the nut.  The bolt was popped out of the cylinder ear.  A new bolt assembly was installed, the valve clearance adjusted, the main oil screen inspected with no contamination found and the engine was returned to service.

A08W0164: The Conair Canadair CL-215, registration C-GFSN, was in climb out of Slave Lake, Alberta, when the no. 1 engine (Pratt & Whitney USA R-2800, WASP CA3) began to backfire. The engine was shut down and the aircraft returned to Slave Lake. Maintenance found a cracked exhaust ear on the no. 2 cylinder. The cylinder was replaced, the engine was ground run and the aircraft was returned to service.

operation: AIR TRANSPORT; FIRE FIGHTING / FIRE MANAGEMENT
Summary: A08Q0178: Le CL215T, immatriculé C-GQBF, effectuait une envolée selon les règles de vol aux instruments entre l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage Int'l et la zone Novembre dans la région de Québec. Il avait été autorisé à 5,000 pieds mais a poursuivi sa montée jusqu'à 5,400 pieds. Une perte de séparation est survenue lorsque l'appareil s'est rapproché à 600 pieds verticalement et 1.4 NM latéralement d'un Airbus 319, opérant sous l'indicatif ACA7021 qui se trouvait en palier à 6,000 pieds en vent arrière droit pour la piste 24. La norme d'espacement requise était de 1,000 pieds ou 3 NM.

A08Q0186: The Airbus A320, registration C-FMSX, was on the initial climb out of CYUL Montreal Pierre Elliott Trudeau Int'l for CYYZ Toronto LBP Int'l when the crew received a fire warning in the aft hold. The fire bottles were discharged, an emergency was declared and the aircraft returned to land CYUL. Runway 06L/24R was closed for a period of 15 minutes while fire crews checked for heat and fire; no signs of smoke or fire were found. Smoke detectors (SDCU), fire bottles and squibs were replaced as per the maintenance manuals. Aircraft returned to service.

A09P0007:  The Air Canada regional (Jazz) CRJ aircraft, C-FDJA, operating as JZA460, took off from Vancouver for Fort McMurray.  During the climb, about 90 nm north of Vancouver the crew received a cargo smoke warning, followed shortly after by a cargo fan fail message.  The crew completed the QRH checklist, discharged the cargo fire suppression bottles, declared an emergency, and returned to Vancouver, where the aircraft landed on runway 26R without further difficulty, with ARFF on standby.  The cargo smoke warning persisted for about 5 minutes after activation.

A09P0101: The Conair Convair 340 aircraft, C-FKFA, operating as CRC454T, was returning to land at Abbotsford, BC after a training flight. When the landing gear was selected down, the left main did not indicate that it was locked. The crew completed all the appropriate checklists but was unable to get a locked indication. They checked the left gear position visually and a company aircraft flew alongside for a visual check. All indications were that the gear was down, but no positive lock could be established. The crew requested ARFF to be activated and landed on runway 25 without further event. The aircraft was stopped on the runway, the pins inserted, and the aircraft taxied to the ramp.

A09Q0062: Un CL215 exploité par le Gouvernement du Québec sous l'indicatif QUE237 effectuait un vol d'entrainement selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB). L'appareil a subi une panne hydraulique et une urgence a été déclarée. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre et a été immobilisé sur la piste pour être ensuite remorqué au hangar. L'appareil n'a subi aucun dommage et il n'y a eu aucun blessé. Les vérifications après le vol ont révélé pompe hydraulique défectueuse.

A09Q0075: The Quebec Government CL215 water bomber, registration C-FTXK, was 10 nm northwest of the CYQB VOR at 5000 ft on a training flight when the right engine (Pratt & Whitney PW 2800) backfired three times. After checking the engine parameters and adjusting the mixture to full rich, the engine ran smoothly. The flight was continued until the right engine backfired again while executing low speed manoeuvres and simulated engine failures in cruise flight. The crew elected to shut the engine down and feather the propeller. All checks were executed and the crew requested the presence of emergency vehicles. The aircraft landed normally at CYQB and taxied under its own power to the company hangar. A maintenance inspection revealed a problem with the ignition system. The engine was repaired and returned to service.

A09W0086: The Conair Firecat, registration C-GABC, had departed Dawson City, Yukon, on a fire dispatch. During initial climb the #2 engine oil temperature began to increase and the oil pressure decreased correspondingly. Power was reduced and level flight was established. The temperature and pressure indications continued toward limits so the retardant load was jettisoned in a safe location and the #2 engine (Curtiss Wright 982C9HE2) was shut down. The aircraft returned to Dawson City, where a single engine landing was accomplished without incident. Maintenance determined that an engine change was required.

A09W0091: After the landing gear on the Conair Aviation Firecat, registration C-GWUP, was selected down on approach to the Whitehorse airport, YT the gear position indicators showed both main gear down and the nose gear up. The pilot broke off the approach, confirmed the hydraulic pressure was correct, and cycled the gear twice. The nose gear position indicator continued to display a nose gear up condition; however, visual observation by ground personnel, and by the pilot by way of a reflective mirror on the left cowling, indicated the nose gear was extended. The landing was accomplished without further incident with ARFF standing by. Maintenance determined that the nose gear uplock switch striker assembly was seized. When the striker assembly was freed and lubricated the nose gear position indicator functioned normally.

A09W0088: The Air Tractor Inc 802A-003 "Fire Boss" tanker, registration N1546H, was engaged in water bombing activity on a fire near Nojack, AB. The single engine aircraft was fitted with Wipair 10 000 amphibious which had been modified to facilitate water scooping. While transiting from the fire to nearby Chip Lake at 500 to 600 feet above ground the engine (Pratt and Whitney PT6A-67AG) surged and flamed out. The pilot selected the flaps and landing gear down, completed a 180, and landed toward the west in the eastbound lane of Highway 16. Both nose-gear legs were down and locked prior to touchdown; however, there was insufficient time for the main gear actuators to extend fully and both main gear collapsed at touchdown. The keel sections of both floats and the bulkheads adjacent to the main gear wells sustained minor damage. The pilot was uninjured.The fuel filters, engine chip plugs, and engine oil filter were examined on site after the incident and no discrepancies which would have contributed to a sudden loss of engine power were identified. Fuel samples taken from the wings and collector tank were clean. The engine started and ran normally after the incident. The aircraft was de-fuelled after the ground run and found to contain approximately 175 liters of fuel. It was estimated that the fuel on board at the time of the incident was sufficient for approximately 50 minutes of flight.The AT-802A is fitted with two wing tanks that are interconnected through a collector tank, and fuel is free to flow between the wing tanks through the collector tank. The AT-802A Airplane Flight Manual emphasizes the importance of keeping the fuel level equalized in each wing tank, especially when the quantity gets down to one-half and below, as the engine can flame if one tank is run dry even if there is a substantial amount of fuel in the other tank. Air Tractor Inc. Service Letters 178 and 178A also address the issue of fuel imbalance. Fuel has a tendency to migrate to the right tank due to torque effects in normal flight, and fuel migration may increase in either direction during bombing action, where a succession of tight turns may result in a significant imbalance. When necessary, pilots balance their fuel tank loads by flying slightly uncoordinated. Fuel migrates in the same direction that the ball indicates in the slip indicator. The fuel gauge was indicating 1/4 to 1/2 on the right tank and 1/8 to 1/4 on the left tank prior to the incident, and the pilot was attempting to balance the gauge readings by holding aircraft was in uncoordinated straight and level flight, with the right wing high, when the engine lost power. The aircraft was fitted with a single fuel gauge with a switch to select the tank to be displayed. It was not fitted with a low fuel light. The rest of the Conair Air Tractor fleet has two independent fuel gauges and a low quantity fuel light. The operator has determined that the right tank quantity indication was over reading significantly. The fuel imbalance associated with the lower than indicated fuel state of the right tank allowed air to be drawn into the engine through the collector tank, resulting in engine flameout. The aircraft was on lease to Conair. The fuel quantity indication system had been calibrated on 01 May 2009, prior to Conair taking delivery of the aircraft. The aircraft has been ferried to the Conair main base in Abbotsford, BC, where the fuel quantity indication system will be checked and calibrated in accordance with Air Tractor recommendations.

A09P0140:  The Conair S2P Firecat aircraft, C-GHPJ, operating as CRC571, took off from Kamloops runway 08 for a fire suppression mission.  Shortly after take-off the no. 1 engine (Wright 1820) oil temperature rose rapidly while the oil pressure reduced.  The pilot released the fire retardent load, feathered the no. 1 engine and returned to Kamloops, where the aircraft landed on runway 08 without further event.

A09W0094: The Conair Group Inc. Douglas DC-6B, C-GKUG, had departed Dawson City, YT to conduct forest fire suppression work. While setting cruise power, approximately 5 nm north of the airport, the No. 4 engine, (Pratt & Whitney-USA, WASP CB3) backfired on auto-lean. When the mixture was set to rich, the engine ran smoothly. The flight crew decided to feather the engine and return to Dawson City where an uneventful three engine approach and landing was completed. Maintenance determined that a crack developed around the exhaust ear on the No. 4 cylinder. An SDR has been filed with TC.

A09P0152:  The Conair Firecat aircraft, C-GHPJ, operating as CRC571, was engaged in fire management operations 35 nm southwest of Kamloops when a company aircraft observed oil trailing from the no. 1 engine.  The pilot looked and saw fluid trailing from the rear of the left nacelle.  He jettisoned the fire retardant load, shut down and secured the no. 1 engine, and returned to Kamloops, where the aircraft landed without further event, with ARFF standing by.  Maintenance inspection found an oil leak from the rocker box oil drain tube.  The tube was replaced, the oil replesnished and the aircraft was returned to service.

A09W0101: The Air Spray (1967) Ltd. Lockheed L188C, C-GZCF, was operating on a fire suppression mission as flight ASP490. While in cruise the flight crew observed the No. 1 TIT fluctuating between 750 and 830°C with associated horsepower fluctuations. The propeller RPMs were stable. The flight crew consulted the abnormal check list and carried out a precautionary shutdown of the No. 1 engine (Allison 501-D13). The aircraft returned to Grande Prairie, AB where an uneventful three engine approach and landing was conducted with ARFF standing by. Maintenance were unable to replicate the problem and released the aircraft back to service.

A09P0154:  The Air Spray L-188 aircraft, C-GZVM, was engaged in fire suppression operations 40 nm west of Campbell River when the crew noticed smoke coming from the electrical bay.  They jettisoned 20 % of the retardant load, completed the QRH electrical smoke drill items, and diverted to Campbell River.  Since they were only 7 minutes from Campbell River they decided not to complete the checklist items for electrical smoke.  The aircraft landed at Campbell River without further event.  Maintenance determined that a phase sync box was the smoke source.  Two phase sync boxes were replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

A09C0093: TKR255, a Canadair CL-215, registration C-FTXI took off from the Thompson, Manitoba airport. During the initial climb the landing gear was selected up and the nose gear did not retract. The crew decided to return to the airport, but continued to fly and burn off fuel in order to meet the landing weight restriction. The crew could not determine whether the nose gear was locked and declared an emergency. The aircraft then landed and stopped on the runway where a ground lock was installed. The aircraft then  taxied back to the hangar without further incident. The nose gear hydraulic selector valve was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

A09W0110: The Conair Firecat C-GWUP had departed a fire near Pelly Crossing, YT, when a vibration in the No. 1 engine was felt. All gauge indications were normal, however the crew decided to complete a precautionary shutdown of the engine (Curtiss Wright 982C9HE2, s/n PC10209C). The aircraft diverted to Whitehorse (CYXY), where maintenance determined that three cylinders had failed. The engine was two hours into a 100-hour extension before overhaul.

A09C0102: The Ontario Ministry of Natural Resources Dehavilland DHC-6, C-FOPI, was on a water bombing run in the vicinity of Red Lake, ON. As the water was dropped at 100 ft over the fire a loud bang was heard. No airborne objects were observed by the crew during the water bombing run. The aircraft continued to fly normally and there were no abnormal indications or vibrations. Post flight examination revealed damage to the leading edge, strut, and flap of the starboard wing and the starbord empennage surface. Maintenance inspection found evidence of bird strikes.

A09Q0097: Le CL215 immatriculé C-FTXG opérant sous l'indicatif QUE228 pour le Service Aérien Gouvernemental du Québec effectuait une mission de lutte des incendies dans la région de Val D'or (Québec). Alors que l'appareil se trouvait à 22 milles nautique au Nord Est, à 4,000 pieds en descente pour l'aéroport de Val D'or, l'équipage a déclaré un urgence après avoir fermé un de ses deux moteurs (Pratt & Whitney Double Wasp CA3). L'équipage a refusé l'assistance des services d'urgence et l'appareil s'est posé sans problème. L'équipe de maintenance a déterminé que la tête d'un cylindre du moteur droit s'était fissurée.

A09Q0105: Le Bombardier CL215T opéré par le Service Aérien du Québec sous l'indicatif de vol QUE247 venait de décoller de CYZV pour un vol d'entrainement.  Au décollage la roue de nez ne s'est pas escamotée normalement.  L'équipage a déclaré une urgence et revenu atterrir sans problème. L'entretien a procédé a un ajustement des micro contacts confirmant l'orientation centrée de la roue de nez et l'appareil a été remis en service.

A09P0195:  The Air Spray Lockheed L-188 aircraft, C-FLJO, was maneouvering on the ground at Victoria, positioning to take on a load of fire retardant, when one wing tip struck the rudder of a parked Conair PA-60-600 aircraft, C-GUHK.  C-FLJO sustained minor damage to one wing tip while C-GUHK sustained minor damage to its rudder.  There were no injuries.

A09P0217:  The Erickson Air Crane Sikorsky S-64E, C-GJZK, was engaged in fire-fighting operations on a fire 10 nm SW of Kelowna.  While snorkeling water from a dip site the left seat pilot noticed small oil spots on the water surface.  Each pilot checked his side of the helicopter for oil leaks with nothing found, and instruments indicated normal operating temperatures and pressures.  The crew decided to jettison the water already picked up and depart the dip site to the west so that the situation could be assessed.  The Master Caution, MGB oil temperature and MGB oil pressure warning lights then illuminated.  The MGB oil pressure indicated zero and the MGB oil temperature indicated greater than 150 degrees C.  An immediate landing was carried out on a logging road and the helicopter was shut down without the auxilliary power pack because of the unknown condition of the upper deck.

A09P0212:  The Conair Firecat S2P aircraft, C-GHDY, operating as CRC573, took off from Kamloops on a fire supression mission.  As climb power was being set the no. 1 engine (Wright Cyclone 982-C9HE2) RPM rapidly increased.  The pilot retarded the no. 1 throttle and set the no. 1 prop lever to course pitch.  The RPM was brought under control at 2450 RPM.  The load of retartdant was jetissoned and the aircraft returned to Kamloops, where it landed without further event.

A09P0213:  The Conair Air Tractor AT-802A, amphibious aircraft, C-FDHY, operating as CRC689, was participating in firefighting activities in the Kelowna area.  The aircraft touched down on Okanagan Lake, in order to scoop water for firefighting, with the landing gear extended. Both floats were ripped off.  The aircraft sank in the lake.  The pilot, the sole occupant, was rescued and was not injured.

A09W0139: The Air Spray Lockheed L188C, (C-FLXT) was on a local flight test. After several engine shutdowns and restarts, the No. 1 engine (Allison 501-D13) developed an rpm fluctuation of 400 to 500 rpm. The crew ran the checklist before shutting the engine down as per Company SOP. An uneventful landing was completed. Maintenance found the engine NTS system out of rig.

A09P0216:  The Air Spray Lockheed L-188A aircraft, C-FZCS, was engaged in fire-fighting operations at a fire located 30 nm northeast of Kamloops.  After the fire retardant had been dropped the no. 2 engine (Allison 501-D13) RPM began to fluctuate between 13,300 to 13,500 (normal is 13,820).  The crew completed the appropriate QRH checklist, shut down the no. 2 engine and feathered the propellor.  The aircraft returned to Kamloops where it completed a one engine inoperative landing, without further event.

A09P0228: The Conair Firecat S2P aircraft, C-GHDY, operating as CRC573, took off from Kamloops on a fire suppression mission. After take-off, the left engine (Curtiss Wright 1820-982C9HE2) CHT began to increase and exceeded the red line. The pilot jettisoned the load of retardent, shut down and secured the engine, and returned to Kamloops, where the aircraft landed without further event. Steel and aluminum fragments were found in the oil screens and both sump plugs. The engine was changed.

A09P0225: A Bell 205A-1, C-GVIJ, operated by Vancouver Island Helicopters, was conducting water bucketing operations for forest fire suppression. The aircraft was in a steep, low-power approach to a small lake to pick up a load of water. The fuel governor RPM Increase/Decrease (beep) switch was set to the lower range of its travel. On the downwind to base leg left turn the pilot raised the collective to arrest the descent and the low rotor RPM horn sounded. The collective was lowered and the horn stopped but the rate of descent increased. The collective was raised again but the rate of descent increased further. As forward cyclic was applied, the bucket impacted the water and jolted the aircraft into a nose down attitude. The pilot applied aft cyclic and more collective which again activated the low rotor RPM warning horn. The aircraft impacted the water in an upright attitude and rolled to the left. When the main rotor struck the water one blade tore off the cabin roof above the right-hand pilot seat. The aircraft sank in about 20 feet of water and was recovered about 1 week later. It was noted that the belly hook release mechanism had not been activated. The pilot (sole person on board) was flying from the left seat and evacuated the aircraft with minor injuries. The helicopter was substantially damaged.

A09P0229:  The Conair Firecat S2P aircraft, C-FEFX, operating as CRC575, was returning to Abbotsford after a fire suppression mission.  Over Chilliwack Lake the right engine (Curtiss Wright 1820-982C9HE2) fire warning light illuminated.  The pilot completed the appropriate QRH checklist, shutdown and secured the engine, and discharged the engine fire bottle.  The aircraft landed on runway 25 at Abbotsford without further event, with ARFF in attendance.  Maintenance inspection determined that oil in the right engine fireloop connectors caused a change in resistance which triggered the fire warning system.

A09P0242:  The Conair Douglas DC-6 aircraft, C-GIBS, operating as CRC451, took off from Abbotsford for Slave Lake, Alberta.  As the aircraft levelled off in cruise, 70 nm north of Abbotsford, the captain noticed low BMEP on #2 engine (PW R2800).  As a precaution, engines 1, 3, 4 were kept at climb power and cruise power was set on #2 which immediately began vibrating and banging.  The mixture was reset to auto-rich on #2 and 1, 3, and 4 were set to METO power.  ATC was advised and the aircraft returned to Abbotsford via radar vectors.  The #2 engine was shut down and the emergency checklist completed.  The aircraft landed on runway 25 at Abbotsford without further difficulty, with ARFF responding.  Maintenance inspection found the #2 cylinder of the #2 engine was cracked.

A09P0249:  The Elbow River Helicopters Bell 212 helicopter, C-GTKE, was engaged in fire-fighting operations about 20 nm south of Lillooet.  While picking up water from the Fraser River with a bucket on a long-line, the helicopter struck the river surface broke-up and sank.  The pilot exited the wreckage and was seen with his head above the water surface, but attempts to rescue him were unsuccessful. THE BOARD AUTHORIZED THE RELEASE OF THIS REPORT ON 19 MARCH 2010.

A09P0267:  The Air Spray Lockheed L-188 aircraft, C-FLJO, operating as ASB482, was engaged in forest-fire management operations out of Williams Lake.  While returning from a mission the no. 4 engine (Allison 501-D13) RPM drooped to 13,600 (normal is 13,850).  As the crew commenced the relevant QRH checklist, the RPM drooped further to 13,450 and the engine began surging.  The engine was shutdown and secured.  The aircraft landed at Williams Lake without further event.  Maintenance changed the prop governor and after a ground run, returned the aircraft to service.On the next flight, shortly after take-off, the no. 4 engine again began surging with RPM and horsepower fluctuations.  The no. 4 engine was shutdown and secured, and the aircraft returned to Williams Lake, where it landed without further event.

A09W0166: The Remote Helicopters AS350B2, C-GRHJ, had landed in a clearing near the fire zone with a crew of four firefighters. The crew disembarked with their gear while the pilot kept the rotor turning with about 40 per cent torque. Two crew remained on the left hand side of the helicopter with the gear while the other two crew members were laying out a longline on the right-hand side of the helicopter. The helicopter suddenly started to roll to the right, resulting in the pilot lifting off. The aircraft then rotated through one or more rotations before the pilot was able to land, heading in the original direction but about 10 feet to the right of his original location. There were no injuries, but the helicopter was substantially damaged; primarily in the tail boom and tail rotor areas. The tail rotor had contacted the ground about four feet from the crew on the right-hand side.

A09P0310:  A Black Tusk Helicopters Bell 214B-1, C-FZVT, was bucketing, topping up water storage tanks at 6,000 feet asl.  While over a tank there was a loud bang and a reduction in power.  The aircraft reached a near-by pad but landed heavily, spreading the skid gear.  There were no injuries.  The long line was not released.

operation: AIR TRANSPORT; FIRE FIGHTING / FIRE MANAGEMENT
Summary: A10A0015: I-DPCR, an Italian Canadair CL-215T, had departed Runway 29 at St. John's NL en route to Lajes airport, Azores Islands. The aircraft had been cleared for the SID 3 departure which requires the aircraft to maintain runway heading to 5000 feet ASL. Just after departure, the aircraft turned left toward the RONPO North Atlantic Track coast out point. The controller immediately issued instructions to the crew of I-DPCR to turn to a heading of 290 degrees. CHI31, a Cougar Helicopters Sikorsky S92, has departed Runway 20 climbing runway heading. Separation between the two aircraft did not erode to less than the required three nm lateral separation, however, safety was not assured.

A10P0095:  The Conair Canadair CL215 aircraft, C-GFSN, took off from abbotsford for a test flight.  While in cruise flight in a left turn over Harrison Mills, the left engine (P&W R2800) started surging.  BMEP fluctuated between 0 and 100.  RPM surged up to 200 RPM.  Other engine parameters were normal.  The crew shut down and secured the engine as a precaution.  The aircraft then returned to Abbotsford where it landed without further event.

A10A0041: A Grumman TBM-3E aircraft operated by Forest Protection Limited departed Runway 09 at the Miramichi Airport (CYCH) for a local training flight. About 1340 ADT, on the downwind leg, the aircraft went into a gradual descent and collided with the terrain. It came to rest on the south side of the airport on the edge of an industrial area. The pilot was fatally injured and the aircraft was destroyed.

A10W0061: The Air Spray L188, registered C-FVFH, had departed Rocky Mountain House, AB and was working on a fire near Whitecourt, AB when the crew noticed there was no hydraulic pressure in the #1 system. They flew back to the Rocky Mountain House area and consulted their dispatch. Due to the fact that the #1 hydraulic system controls ground steering and brakes, the decision was made to go to Edmonton Intl. airport because of the runway oriented winds. An emergency was declared and an uneventful landing took place. The aircraft was then returned to service.

operation: AIR AMBULANCE/ EMERGENCY MEDICAL; FIRE FIGHTING / FIRE MANAGEMENT
Summary: A10O0077: The Heli-Excel Bell 205A-1 helicopter (C-GLHE) was dispatched to a local fire and was climbing out from the helipad at Geraldton airport. The Thunder Airlines Ltd. Mitsubishi MU-2B-60 airplane (C-FRWK) was on final approach to runway 26. The Bell helicopter pilot transmitted on 122.8 that the helicopter was departing and to confirm there was no conflicting traffic in the area. There was no response received and the helicopter proceeded to take-off in a southerly direction across the threshold of runway 26. At approximately 250 feet agl the helicopter pilot noticed the MU-2B-60 on final approach and altered course. The MU2B-60 passed underneath the helicopter with an estimated separation of 150 feet between the two aircraft.

A10P0114:  The Rogers Helicopters Bell 212 helicopter, N212HL, was on final for the helipad at Kamloops airport, after a flight from Omak, Washington when the hydraulic warning light illuminated and the pilot noticed that he had lost hydraulic pressure to the tail rotor, indicating a no. 1 hydraulic system failure.  The pilot continued the approach but was not able to land on the helipad.  The helicopter landed on the ramp without further event.
