An inspection found a leak in the hydraulic hard line from the pump to the oil pressure indicator.  The line was replaced and the helicopter was returned to service.

A10W0071: The Conair CL215, C-GFSN, was engaged in fighting a fire near Slave Lake, AB. While en route from the fire zone to the lake to scoop another load of water, the crew noticed that the LH engine (Pratt & Whitney R2800) oil quantity had decreased to 15 gallons and decreasing steadily. No loss of oil pressure was noted. A precautionary engine shutdown was completed and the aircraft returned to Slave Lake for an uneventful landing. Maintenance found that the plug had fallen out of the threaded access hole used for pe-oiling the engine.

A10C0066: The Saskatchewan Government DeHavilland CS2F-2 Tracker, registration C-GEQE operating as TKR506, was departing Prince Albert, SK. The pilot rejected the take-off at rotation after detecting smoke in the cockpit. The aircraft stopped on the runway safely after the retardant load was dumped. Information provided indicated that the smoke was likely hydraulic mist from a hose leak in the fire bombing system.

A10Q0083: Le Bell 204B immatriculé C-FOKY en exploitation commerciale, effectuait une opération d'arrosage héliporté sur le feu 284 situé à environ 7 miles marins (nm) au sud-est du barrage Gouin. Lors d'un remplissage de la citerne en utilisant une longue élingue de 100 pieds, l'appareil s'est mis à tourner en sens horaire. Le pilote a largué la citerne et a repris la maîtrise directionnelle de l'appareil. Un atterrissage a été effectué sur une piste de gravier située à environ 4 nm au nord-ouest avec une vitesse  d'environ 20 k. L'appareil s'est immobilisé sur la piste, n'a subi aucun dommage et il n'y a eu aucun blessé. L'inspection a révélé la défaillance du " Crosshead Bearing " P/N 204-011-761-003 entrainant le remplacement du Crosshead assy P/N 204-011-711-001, du slider P/N 204-011-711-001, du Tube assy P/N 204-011-711-001, du tail rotor control sprocket P/N 204-010-740-005 et de la chain assy P/N 205-001-721-001.

A10P0157:  The Conair Convair 580 aircraft, C-FKFL, operating as CRC449, was operating out of Prince George on a fire suppression mission.  After dropping the fire retardant, in accordance with the after bomb checklist the crew selected the hydraulic bypass switch up whereupon the gear unsafe light illuminated.  Through troubleshooting the crew was able to establish that the gear unsafe light only illuminated when the hydraulic bypass was up.  During the return to Prince George with the bypass up and the light on, the light extinguished.  The aircraft landed at Prince George without further event with ARFF in attendance.  Maintenance traced the problem to micro switch misadjustment.  All three gear micro switches were readjusted and the aircraft was returned to service.

A10C0092: The Manitoba Government Air Services Canadair CL215, registration C-GUMW operating as TKR251 was returning to Flin Flon, MB, after releasing its load on a fire suppression mission. There was an engine back fire and a drop in manifold pressure on one of the engines (Pratt & Whitney R-2800). The crew shut the engine down and continued for a safe landing at Flin Flon. Maintenance inspection revealed a carburetor problem.

A10C0095: A Convair 580A, C-GSKR, operated by Saskatchewan Government Northern Air Operations as flight T471, was conducting fire fighting operations. Max power was selected after holding the load on a bombing run. Seconds later, the crew observed a master caution light and the right engine (Allison 501) flamed out. The crew carried out checklist procedures, departed from the fire area, and determined the engine shutdown had resulted from the autofeather being armed. The crew carried out an air start of the right engine, and returned to La Ronge without further incident.

A10C0119: The Canadair CL-215, C-FTUV, was scooping water at Tullibe Lake, MB, for fire supression purposes when the crew noted fluctuating manifold pressure and a drop in Brake Mean Effective Pressure (BMEP) on the left engine. The water load was jettisoned and the aircraft climbed to 2300 ft asl when the left engine (Pratt & Whitney R2800 Sn 27383) backfired and lost all power. The crew shut down the engine and diverted to Thompson where they carried out an uneventful landing. An inspection revealed a damaged #2 cylinder intake valve. The #2 cylinder and valve were replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

A10W0105: The Ultra Helicopters Ltd. AS350BA helicopter, C-FXMJ, landed in a clearing about 50 nm north of Wabasca, AB to pick up a fire crew. After liftoff and acceleration through 30 knots, a main rotor vibration was detected, and the aircraft was landed in a clearing about 800 meters away. Two main rotor blades had sustained substantial damage in the trim tab area, likely from contact with a tree. The helicopter was grounded on-site, and due to fading daylight, the pilot and four passengers were extracted the next day.

A10C0130: The Canadair CL-215 aircraft, registration C-FTUV was carrying out a fire supression operation in the vicinity of Gillam, MB. While manoeuvering, the left engine (P&W R2800) lost all power. The crew secured the engine and began a return trip to the Thompson airport. While in flight, the right generator failed and the crew decided to proceed back to Gillam. The aircraft landed without further incident. The left engine carburetor throttle arm and the right generator had both failed.

A10W0123: The Conair Firecat, C-FOPU, was conducting fire suppression operations 50 nm south of Watson Lake, YT when the No. 2 engine (Curtis Wright 1820, 982C9HE2) started to run roughly. The pilot jettisoned the load and shutdown the No. 2 engine. An uneventful single-engine approach and landing was conducted in Watson Lake. Maintenance found that the No. 1 cylinder valve heads had broken off their valve stems causing extensive damage to the cylinder, piston and connecting rod.

A10P0242:  The Transwest Helicopters Ltd. Bell 214B-1 helicopter (registration C-GTWV, serial number 28048), with 2 pilots onboard, was engaged in firefighting operations approximately 20 nautical miles northwest of Lillooet, British Columbia. At 1124 Pacific Daylight Time, after refilling the water bucket, the helicopter was on approach to its target near a creek valley. As the helicopter slowed and started to descend past a ridgeline into the creek valley, the engine lost power. The pilot-in-command, seated in the left-hand seat, immediately turned the helicopter left to climb back over the ridgeline to get to a clearing, released the water bucket and the 130-foot long-line from the belly hook, and descended toward an open area to land. The helicopter touched down hard on uneven, sloping terrain, and pitched over the nose. When the advancing main-rotor blade contacted the ground, the airframe was in a near-vertical, nose-down attitude, which then rotated the fuselage, causing it to land on the left side. A small post-crash fire ignited. The pilot-in-command sustained a concussion and was rendered unconscious. The copilot escaped with minor injuries and dragged the pilot-in-command from the wreckage. The pilot-in-command regained consciousness a few minutes later. The helicopter was substantially damaged. The 406-megahertz emergency locator transmitter was activated, but its antenna fitting fractured; as a result, the search and rescue satellite network did not receive a signal.UPDATE: 12 MAY 2020

A10P0244: On 31 July 2010 at 2002 Pacific Daylight Time, Conair Group Inc.'s Convair 580 (registration C-FKFY, serial number 129) operating as Tanker 448 departed Kamloops to fight a wildfire near Lytton, British Columbia. The bombing run required crossing the edge of a ravine in the side of the Fraser River canyon before descending on the fire located in the ravine. About 22 minutes after departure, Tanker 448 approached the ravine and struck trees. An unanticipated retardant drop occurred coincident with the tree strikes. Seconds later, Tanker 448 entered a left-hand spin and collided with terrain. A post-impact explosion and fire consumed much of the wreckage. A signal was not received from the on-board emergency locator transmitter; nor was it recovered. Both crew members were fatally injured.

A10P0259:  The Yellowhead Helicopters Bell 407 helicopter, C-FYHY, was engaged in fire-fighting operations 25 nm north of Mcbride, and was on approach to a landing on a road to deliver some supplies.  As the helicopter hovered and settled a fine dust was blown up from the road, the pilot lost visual reference and drifted to his 8 o'clock position.  He heard a thump and assuming a blade strike, he aborted the landing and proceeded to a pad one kilometer distant.  A post flight inspection found blade delamination and other evidence of main rotor damage.  The main rotor and mast were removed and sent for examination by the manufacturer.  The pilot was not injured.

A10P0275:  The Wildcat Helicopters Bell 212, C-FOHK, was engaged in forest fire fighting operations 30 nm SSW of Williams Lake.  While lowering the bucket into a pond to fill it, the no. 1 engine (PWC PT6-3B) spooled down.  The pilot transitioned to forward flight and jettisoned the bucket and long line, whereupon the no. 1 fire handle illuminated. The pilot pulled the no. 1 fire handle, closed the throttle and shut off the fuel valve.  The pilot transmitted a distress message on the radio and was advised by another helicopter that there was no sign of smoke.  The fire handle light then extinguished and after a few seconds the ITT began to decrease.  As the fire was out and the helicopter was flying well on the no. 2 engine, the pilot elected to divert to Williams Lake, where the helicopter landed without further event.  A catastrophic failure of the no. 1 engine power section was found.  The no. 1 engine was replaced.  The no. 2 engine was inspected, boroscoped, and power checked for indications of stress with no faults found, and the helicopter was returned to service.

A10P0278: A Martin JRM3, C-FLYL, operated by Coulson Flying Tankers, was engaged in fire fighting operations at Fraser Lake, BC. The aircraft, with four crew members on board, had touched down on the lake and was scooping water when an overspeed of the #4 engine (Wright Cyclone 3350-24, s/n 474859) occurred. The take-off was rejected without further incident. The engine and propeller (Curtis Electric C644S-B314, s/n 156150) were changed and sent for examination due to the overspeed.

A11P0028: Shortly after take off from Runway 13 at Courtenay Airpark, at about 50 feet altitude, the amateur-built Van's RV-4 engine (Lyc. O-320D2A) stopped. The pilot headed straight ahead and landed hard along the shoreline. The main landing gear was damaged, and the propeller struck the ground.  The tide was low at the time and the aircraft was out of the water. The RCMP and fire crews responded. The aircraft was moved to keep it out of the water at high tide. The pilot observed some white crystalline substance in suspension when he dipped the tanks during an earlier stop at Port Alberni, and noted a relatively dark blue tint to the fuel from that location.The engine and fuel system will be examined further to assess any possible fuel blockage or contamination.

A11C0076: The Delta Helicopters Aerospatiale AS350 BA, C-GVXA, was bucketing water in support of fire fighting operations near Meadow Lake, Saskatchewan. The winds were gusting out the SSE at 20 to 30 knots. The pilot was flying slowly just above tree top level in order to dump a load of water on a fire break area, when the nose of the helicopter suddenly swung to the left. The pilot added power, but the rotation increased. The pilot reduced power and lowered the collective. The helicopter entered the trees and came to rest on its right side with the tail boom separated from the helicopter. The pilot was transported to the Meadow Lake hospital and kept overnight for observation.

A11W0070: The Campbell Helicopters Ltd. Bell 212, C-FJUR, serial number 30728, was conducting water bucketing operations in support of forest fire suppression services in the vicinity of Slave Lake, Alberta. At approximately 1449 Mountain Daylight Time, during an approach to Lesser Slave Lake to pick up water, the helicopter crashed into the lake on its right side. Within minutes, the pilot was removed from the wreckage by forest fire fighters working on the shoreline. The forest fire fighters administered first aid until emergency medical personnel arrived. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was fatally injured. There was no post-crash fire; however, the helicopter sustained major damage. The emergency locator transmitter signal was not detected by search and rescue until the helicopter was removed from the water.

A11W0077: A Conair Group Douglas DC-6B, C-GKUG, was on a fire suppression flight when a line of white smoke from the number 1 engine (Pratt & Whitney R-2800) was observed by the accompanying bird-dog aircraft after a drop. The engine was shut down and C-GKUG returned to Dawson City, Yukon. Maintenance identified a crack in the number 3 cylinder.

A11A0027: The Lufthansa Airbus A340-311, registration D-AIGB, was operating as DLH420 on a flight from Frankfurt, Germany to Boston, MA when the flight crew received the ECAM message "SMOKE CAB REST SMOKE"; indication of possible fire in the aircraft's mobile crew rest area (MCR). Since the area was occupied, the flight crew established communication with the rest crew to confirm that the fire warning was not accidentally triggered. No smoke or fire was observed but one of the rest crew thought a smell could be detected briefly.  The MCR was evacuated and the flight crew activated the fire extinguishing system, declared an emergency, and obtained a clearance to descend to FL250 and divert to the nearest airport, Goose Bay, NL. The cabin was prepared for an emergency landing and passengers were re-briefed on evacuation procedures. The flight continued to Goose bay and landed without incident with ARFF standing by.The aircraft was shutdown to allow fire crew to inspect the MCR and when no sign of heat or combustion could be detected, the aircraft was restarted and taxied to ramp where passengers deplaned normally. Maintenance personnel inspected the MCR and adjacent cargo compartment and passenger cabin areas for evidence of heat or combustion without any sign being detected.  A smoke detection control unit inspection was performed without fault and the system was reset.  The MCR was blocked according to MEL for the return flight to Frankfurt. The flight back to Frankfurt was without any problem.Further trouble shooting was performed after arrival in Frankfurt in conjunction with a detailed action order without fault and the aircraft was returned to service.

A11C0109: A Canadair CL215T, C-FAWQ operated by the Quebec Government as flight QUE239, was conducting firefighting operations when the crew identified a problem with the rudder control system. The crew carried out abnormal checklist procedures and reverted to rudder manual mode. The flight diverted to Dryden and landed without further incident. Company maintenance replaced the rudder hydraulic actuator (P/N 215T-92255-2) and the aircraft returned to service.

A11W0103: The Buffalo Airways Douglas DC-4, C-FBAP, was approximately 30 nm out from the Yellowknife, NT VOR on a 275° bearing, having departed from Hay River, NT. The crew detected a slight vibration in the #2 engine (Pratt & Whitney USA R2000-7M2). It was shut down as a precautionary measure, and the flight returned to Hay River. Maintenance has removed the engine and will report to the TSB on its findings.Update 27 July: Suspect a top end failure, ie piston. Aluminium was found in screen, temps and pressures normal.

A11W0126: The Mustang Helicopters Eurocopter AS350-B2, C-FMNE, had departed Livingston Gap Fire Base in Alberta and was approximately 5 miles out when the pilot was alerted by a hydraulic warning light and horn. The hydraulic system was shut off as per the flight manual and the flight returned to the base. Upon coming into a low hover, control was lost and the main rotor blades struck the ground. An upright but hard landing resulted. It was reported that the pilot received a serious injury, and of the 4 passengers on board, one received a minor injury. The operator will report back to the TSB when on scene, and the TSB will follow up with hydraulic system component tests.Update 29 August: The pilot was not injured. Site survey confirmed that the impending bypass indication had popped out on the hydraulic system. The TSB will investigate further.Update 24 Oct: All 3 servos were tested at the Eurocopter Canada facilities under the supervision of a TSB investigator. In addition the hydraulic pump and belt, pressure sending unit, tank and wiring harness were inspected. Other than expected bendingwith the resultant binding from the impact, all servos operated within normal parameters. The other components had no anomalies.

A11C0169: While in cruise flight enroute from Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario to Thompson, Manitoba the crew of Buffalo Airways flight TKR281, a Canadair CL215 C-GDKY, noticed a sudden power loss indication on the right hand Pratt & Whitney R2800 engine. The crew carried out a precautionary engine shutdown and feather and diverted to Pickle Lake, Ontario. Following landing the right hand engine was unfeathered and run to determine the problem as instructed by maintenance. A 2" waiver was noticed in the manifold pressure reading. The aircraft was secured and is awaiting maintenance action.

A11A0085: The Provincial Airlines Ltd. Saab 340A aircraft (registration C-FPAI) was operating as SPR908 on a flight from St. Anthony, NL (CYAY) to St. John's, NL (CYYT). While en-route to CYYT, a burning smell was noticed. The crew shut off the recirculation fans and consulted the QRH checklist after which the smell seemed to dissipate. When the smell was again noted, the crew elected to divert to Gander, NL (CYQX) and declared an emergency shortly thereafter. The burning smell dissipated once more and the flight landed without incident at CYQX with ARFF crews standing by. Fire crews confirmed that no indication of fire was present and followed the aircraft as it taxied to the terminal where the passengers deplaned normally. Company maintenance inspected the aircraft, replaced the right air cycle machine (ACM) for a suspected bearing failure and returned the aircraft to service.

A12P0035: Conair Convair C-FFKFA (ser 100). The aircraft was conducting a routine flight near the Abbottsford airport (CYXX) when the crew noticed what might be smoke in both the cockpit and the main cabin.  The crew decided to return to base in CYXX and communicated with ATC that they had smoke in the cockpit. After completing the emergency checklist the aircraft landed in CYXX with ARFF standing by. There was no damage or injuries, the smoke was suspected to have come from the heater and tail anti-ice ducting.  15 Mar 2012.

A12P0055:  The Conair Convair 580 firetanker, C-FKFA,  was on a VFR approach to Abbotsford, when the flight crew noted a gear unsafe indication. None of the gear-down lights illuminated upon gear down selection. The approach was aborted and the flight crew completed the appropriate abnormal check-list. As a precaution the flight crew declared an emergency. They flew low over on the active runway (Rwy 19) and personnel on the ground confirmed the gear was down. ARFF were on standby and the subsequent landing was uneventful. Precautions were taken before the aircraft was taxiied off the runway. Company maintenance found a broken electrical connection to the landing gear handle microswith.

A12Q0053: Un CL215 exploité par le Gouvernement du Québec sous l'indicatif QUE228 effectuait un vol d'entrainement selon les règles de vols à vue depuis l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) avec deux pilotes à bord. Lors d'une approche pour l'atterrissage, une indication anormale de roue de nez est apparue. L'équipage a déclaré une urgence et a utilisé le système d'urgence pour sortir la roue de nez. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre, n'a subi aucun dommage et il n'y a eu aucun blessé.

A12Q0080: Le CL215T immatriculé C-FAWQ, propriété du Service Aérien Gouvernemental du Québec, effectuait une mission de combat de feu de forêt à partir de l'aéroport Chibougamau/Chapais (CYMT) au Québec. Lors de la montée initiale, l'équipage a reçu une indication que la roue de nez n'était pas centrée. Ils ont exécuté la liste de vérification et ils ont déclaré une urgence. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre. L'équipe de maintenance a remplacé la centering switch et a remis l'appareil en service.

A12C0080: The Province of Saskatchewan flight TKR214, a Canadair CL215-1A10 aircraft, registration C-FYWO, was on a fire suppression flight with a crew of two on board. After dropping a load of water, the crew noticed the right engine (P&W R2800) was leaking oil. The crew decided to do a precautionary shutdown and return to the La Ronge airport. Emergency sevices was put on standby and the aircraft then landed without further incident. It was reported that an oil inhibiting fitting cap had come loose resulting in the oil leak

A12C0089: The Questral Helicopters Eurocopter AS 350 B3 (C-GFUG) was en route to Winnipeg, MB from Brandon, MB on a routine ferry flight. Shortly after departing Brandon the pilot noted a vibration in the rudder pedals. After discussion with an on board maintenance person the decision was made to land and assess the cause of the vibration. During the landing, it was determined that the vibration was coming from the tail rotor (T/R). The flight to Winnipeg, where maintenance would be available, resumed but approximately 20 minutes after lift off the vibration worsened and was accompanied by a noise, and the pilot initiated a precautionary landing near Austin, MB. The maintenance engineer inspected the T/R and noted that the T/R half-shell bearings had failed and that the rotor blade cuff appeared to have separated from the rotor spar.  The helicopter was removed from service and is awaiting replacement parts. On 06 July 2012 the T/R half shell bearings (P/N 704A33-6332-61) on T/R blade (P/N 355A12-0055-00 S/N 18126) were replaced. The aircraft had 91.3 hr. total airframe time.

A12Q0129:Le Cessna 337G, immatriculé C-GJOD et exploité par Sasair effectuait un vol selon les règles du vol à vue avec seul le pilote à  son bord. Lors de l'approche à l'aéroport de Baie Comeau, , le voyant désaccord train d'atterrissage droit s'est illuminé après que le pilote ait sélectionné le train d'atterrissage sorti. L'appareil a effectué une remontée et le personnel au sol a confirmé que le train n'était pas verrouillé. Par la suite, le pilote a déclaré une urgence puis a tenté en vain à plusieurs reprises de régler le problème. Le pilote a fermé les deux moteurs avant d'atterrir sur le ventre dans le gazon sur le côté de la piste. L'appareil a subi des dommages importants au ventre de l'appareil et à l'hélice arrière. Le pilote est sorti indemne de l'accident.

A12A0080: The Government of Newfoundland and Labrador Cessna 337G, registration C-GLFY, was operating on a flight from Goose Bay, NL to Port Hope Simpson (CCP4). Following a normal approach for landing on runway 12 at CCP4, the aircraft bounced in gusty wind conditions and landed hard on the nose landing gear. The aircraft sustained damage requiring repair to the nose landing gear and replacement of number one propeller. Upon further inspection, the operator also replaced the number one engine.

A12Q0134: Le CL-215 (QUE231), immatriculé C-FTXK, propriété du Service Aérien du Gouvernement du Québec, effectuait une envolée selon les règles de vol aux instruments entre l'aéroport de Matagami , Québec (CYNM) et l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage Int'l, Québec (CYQB). Lors de l'envolée, l'appareil a subi un problème électrique de couplage en parallèle relié aux deux génératrices. Par mesure de précaution, l'équipage a demandé d'être acheminé vers l'aéroport de Val-D'Or, Québec (CYVO). Lors de l'approche finale, l'indication de train descendu et verrouillé n'est pas apparue. Une vérification visuelle a été faite et afin de s'assurer que le train était bien en position descendu et verrouillé, l'équipage a utilisé le système de descente du train d'urgence. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre. Un contacteur de verrouillage train sorti sur le train principal gauche a été remplacé. Un permis de vol de convoyage a été émis avec le train d'atterrissage descendu jusqu'à Québec/Jean Lesage Int'l, Québec (CYQB) pour permettre à l'équipe de maintenance d'effectuer des essais de rétraction au sol.

A12W0109: A Black Swan Helicopter Ltd. Bell 204B, C-FOKY, was involved in fire fighting operations east of High Level, Alberta. The main transmission low oil pressure light was observed and the pilot conducted a precautionary landing at the Fox Lake airport. One minute after landing the transmission seized. A post-incident inspection revealed that the retaining bolts of a wafer filter located on the side on the main gear box had not been sufficiently fastened resulting in oil blowing past the seal.Update 18 Sep 2012: TC Maintenance and Manufacturing reported that shortly before this incident maintenance had been conducted by a company contract AME, at which time the wafer filters had been inspected. Post-incident inspection revealed that the transmission had little or no oil remaining, caused from loose wafer filter cover bolts (determined by company maintenance staff). The loose bolts allowed oil pressure to push out the gasket between the filter housing and filter cap allowing oil to be pumped overboard. The oil starved transmission was replaced with a serviceable unit and flown to the company's main base for further investigation.

A12P0137: Just after takeoff from Williams Lake, BC, the crew of the Conair Convair 580, registration C-FKFL (serial #465), operating as flight 449, observed a fire indication warning on the right engine (Allison 501-D13D). The crew reduced power on the affected engine while conducting the emergency checklist and the warning stopped. The right engine was then shut down and an emergency was declared. While maneuvering to land, the retardant load was jettisoned in a wooded area. The aircraft landed without further incident.

A12A0095: The Government of Newfoundland and Labrador Canadair CL-215, registration C-FTXA, was operating on a local training flight from Gander, NL (CYQX) when, while about 70 nm south of the airport, the aircraft lost power in the number one engine. Following the engine (Pratt & Whitney R-2800-83AM) power loss, the aircraft also lost electrical power to navigation equipment and engine instruments. The crew secured the failed engine, contacted CYQX tower and returned to the airport with ARFF standing by. The flight landed without further incident 20 min later.Maintenance personnel inspected the aircraft and determined that fuel supply to number one became interrupted when the engine driven fuel pump drive spline became disengaged from the engine. Three electrical current limiters were found to have failed - believed to have failed when the LH generator came off line and the additional electrical load of the propeller feathering pump was added to number two generator. The current limiters were replaced, the electrical system inspected and tested, and the aircraft was released for service.

A13O0038: Jazz flight JZA7945, a Canadair CL-600-2B19 (C-GJZZ) aircraft, was departing Toronto LBPIA when the flight crew received a lavatory smoke indication along with reports of an electrical burning smell in the cabin. No smoke was visible in the cabin or cockpit. An emergency was declared, the aircraft returned to Toronto and landed without further incident. The aircraft was stopped on a taxiway and inspected by fire crews using IR cameras. No signs if fire or hotspots were detected. The aircraft was cleared to the gate. Maintenance found two burn marks on the back of a light assembly.

A13P0028: At 14:24 PDT (21:24 Z) the Boeing 767-300, JA653J, operated by Japan Airlines as flight JAL17, was planning to depart Vancouver for Narita, Japan (RJAA) when the takeoff from Runway 26L was aborted. The aircraft came to an abrupt stop just west of Runway 12. ARFF was advised. JAL17 exited Runway 26L onto Lima 2 and then held on taxiway Lima and fire crews inspected the brakes. JAL17 was escorted to the deicing bay and water was applied to cool the brakes. All eight main tires deflated. The crew advised ATS that the aborted takeoff was due to a possible bird strike and injestion on the left engine. Fire crews reported possible fan blade damage on left engine. Runway 26L was inspected for debris but nothing was found.

A13P0056:  A Conair Convair 340/580 waterbomber (C-GKFO) flight CRA453T was training near Abbotsford when the crew received an engine fire indication.  The engine was shut down and an emergency declared and the aircraft diverted to Abbotsford. The aircraft landed safely at 10:49 PDT. There were no injuries.  It was determined that the indication was for the fire bottle discharge indication system. Trouble shooting will determine if the fault is in the indication system or the fire bottle system itself.

A13W0059: The Air Spray Ltd. Lockheed L188A, C-FTDH, was on climb out from a forest fire water drop when the #2 propeller (Aeroproducts A6441-606) started to wander and droop.The checklist for wandering prop was completed, and the propeller was monitored closely returning to Slave Lake, AB.Getting closer to Slave Lake, it was evident the prop was not regulated at lower power settings, so the #2 engine (Allison 501-D13) was shutdown as per the company SOP. An uneventful 1 engine inoperative landing was made at Slave Lake airport. Maintenance found that  an O-ring and backup ring combination installed in an internal transfer tube assembly in the propeller hub were reversed. This caused the O-ring to chatter, wear out and leak, which  allowed a drop in propeller governing pressure.

A13C0053: The Saskatchewan Provincial Government tanker 475, a Convair 580 aircraft, registration C-GSKQ departed the Prince Albert airport and was enroute to Meadow Lake, Saskatchewan, While in cruise, the crew noticed a drop in the right engine (Allison 501-D13) power section oil temperature accompanied by a rise in oil pressure. The crew elected to shut the right engine down and returned to the Prince Albert airport where they declared an emergency. The aircraft then landed without further incident. It was reported that start switch was left in the "start" position after engine start, which resulted in the low oil temperature and high oil pressure indications.

A13W0068: An Alpine Helicopters Inc. Bell 212 (C-FAHR) had just picked up an empty water bladder from atop a ridge and was proceeding down the mountain. The pilot observed that the load was unstable and reduced speed in an attempt to stabilize it. As the speed reduced, the bladder became unhooked and fell to the ground. The bladder was recovered and the hook was inspected and no defects were found. Personal were briefed on the use of remote hooks and hooking to the belly of the aircraft.

A13W0091: On approach to Hay River, NT a Buffalo Airways Ltd. McDonnell-Douglas DC-4 (C-FBAP), operating as TKR15, shut down the number 2 engine (Pratt & Whitney-USA R2000-7M2) due to fluctuating fuel pressure. No emergency was declared.A post incident inspection found that the AN-4 line from the heater fuel supply fitting on the number 2 boost pump was loose. The line was secured and the aircraft was returned to service.

A13A0065: The Forest Protection Cessna 337 (registration C-GXMA) aeroplane departed Bathurst with one crew and one passenger. After a 1 hour 40 minutes the flight returned for landing. There was a slight crosswind and the aircraft bounced upon landing, ballooned then landed hard on the nose wheel. The front tire blew and the front propellor struck the runway. The front engine was shutdown and the aircraft taxiied clear of the runway using rear engine power. A new front tire and rim are required, the front propellor will need replacing and the front engine inspected / overhauled.

A13A0075: The Government of Newfoundland and Labrador Air Services Division Bombardier CL-415 amphibious aircraft (C-FIZU), operating as Tanker 286, departed Wabush, Newfoundland and Labrador, to fight a nearby forest fire. Shortly after departure, Tanker 286 touched down on Moosehead Lake to scoop a load of water. About 40 seconds later a left hand turn was initiated and almost immediately there was a lost of control. The aircraft water-looped and came to rest upright but partially submerged.  There was an insufficient forward impact force to activate the onboard 406 MHz emergency locator transmitter. There were no injuries to the 2 crew members. The aircraft was destroyed.

A13C0086: A Provincial Helicopters Bell 206L-1, C-GMHK (S/N 45286), was being used in support of forest fire operations in and around Sherridon, MB accompanied by a Manitoba Natural Resources safety officer. The pilot had fueled the helicopter at the fueling pad in Sherridon and had lifted off the pad and at approximately 1/4 mile away when the left boost pump caution light illuminated. The pilot initiated a return to the fueling pad when the engine suddenly flamed out. The pilot conducted an autorotation into a clear area near the shoreline of a lake. As the helicopter began to settle the pilot rolled the helicopter onto its right side to clear the rotor blades from the fuselage. The pilot and passenger exited without injury. The operator is in the process of recovering the helicopter and will transport it back to their main base in Lac du Bonnet, MB for an examination of the fuel system.

A13P0156:  During flight operations out of Penticton BC, the Air Spray L-188 (Electra) C-FVFH had a propeller (AEROPRODUCTS, A6441FN-606) overspeed to pitch lock then to fuel topping.  The engine(ALLISON, 501-D13) was shut down and the aircraft returned to Penticton. The propeller was worked on in Penticton and the next day the problem reoccurred.  The aircraft then procceeded to Red Deer were the propeller was changed.

A13P0163:  The VIH Helicopter Kamov KA32A11BC, Registeration C-GKHL, s/n (31594)8891/03, was carring out fire supression operation with a water bucket. Just after lifting a load of water out of a high level mountain lake, there was a bang and the helicopter began to shake violently. The flying pilot headed the helicopter to an emergency landing site, while the non-flying pilot released the external load (line and bucket) with difficulty. They could not get the helicopter to point in the direction they were tracking and while there were no caution lights the shaking was such that they could not see the instrument displays. The helicopter contacted the ground going sideways and rolled on its starboard side. The main-rotor blades contacted the ground and broke. The crew was able to shut the engines off and exit with minor injuries. There was no fire. Update 2014-05-14: Engine powerloss due to CT section failure.

A13C0090: The Cessna 337 aircraft, registration C-FVAS was inbound for runway 06 at the Stony Rapids airport. The aircraft subsequently landed on the runway with the landing gear retracted. The aircraft came to rest on the runway and the crew evacuated the aircraft without injury. The aircraft sustained damage to its belly and front propeller. It was reported that there were no mechanical anomalies with the aircraft and that the landing gear was not extended prior to landing.

A13C0099: The Delta Helicopters Bell 204B, C-GDUK had departed CJW4 Pelican Narrows, Saskatchewan on smoke patrol cruising at 2500 ft. ASL. The aircraft encountered turbulence followed by porpoising accompanied by left and right yawing and strong vibrations. The pilot initiated a descent to an open area on the south end of a lake. During the descent the aircraft began to yaw to the right. The aircraft landed at the shoreline with the front of the skid gear and nose in the water. The helicopter was shut down and evacuated without event. Inspection revealed that a bolt securing the pitch change link to the pitch change horn of one tail rotor blade had failed. The blade had struck the side of the vertical stabilizer (pylon). The helicopter will be recovered from the site for repair. Inspection of the failed bolt indicated that the bolt had failed due to fatigue. There were indications that the bolt had been loose at some time in the past. The operator is changing their maintenance practices to ensure that the bolts are replaced at each tail rotor installation. Bolts will also be replaced if subsequently found to be loose during service.

A13Q0146: Un CL215 immatriculé C-FTXG, exploité par le Gouvernement du Québec sous l'indicatif GRFEU 01 effectuait un vol d'entrainement selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB). Lors de la montée, le moteur (Pratt & Whitney, WASP CA3 R2800) de droite a subi des retours de flamme. Le moteur fut sécurisé et l'hélice mise en drapeau. L'équipage a déclaré une urgence et est revenu se poser à CYQB avec les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs en alerte. L'appareil n'a subi aucun dommage et il n'y a eu aucun blessé.

A13C0106: The Canadair CL215, registration C-GMAK was enroute to The Pas, Manitoba following a fire suppression flight. While enroute, the right engine (PW R2800) began to backfire and run rough. The engine power was reduced but the engine continued to run rough. The crew elected to do a precautionary shut down and continue to The Pas where the aircraft landed without further incident.

A14W0003: The First Air ATR 42-300 (C-FIQU) operating as flight FAB120 from Yellowknife, NT (CYZF) to Hay River, NT (CYHY) was taxiing for departure when the flight attendant noticed smoke and notified the flight crew. The aircraft was taxied back to the ramp and a request for ARFF was made. The crew completed smoke / electrical smoke checklist followed by ramp shutdown checklist. The aircraft was met by fire crew and company maintenance. Smoke had subsided to allow for a normal deplaning of passengers and crew. The source of smoke was identified as a speaker transformer located on left bin #4 which was found burnt and electrically shorted. The transformer has been replaced and an SDR to Transport Canada was submitted.

A14P0011: A DeHavilland DHC-8-311, C-FACV, operated by Jazz from Vancouver to Penticton as Flight JZA8350 was waiting on taxiway 'Lima' to depart runway 08R when a flight attendant noticed the No 1 (left) engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW123, SN PCE123062) was smoking. The flight crew were advised, shutdown both engines, and discharged the fire suppression agent into the left engine compartment. They passed the information to ATC and ARFF responded; they confirmed there was no further indication of fire. The aircraft was towed back to the gate and passengers were off-loaded there.

A14W0083: An Air Spray (1967) Ltd. Lockheed L-188C Electra (C-GHZI) departed High Level, AB (CYOJ) for aerial fire action near Rainbow Lake, AB. During maneuvers, the crew noticed the # 2 engine (Allison, 501-D13) RPM gauge was reading 13200 rpm where a minimum of 13400 rpm is required. Flight crew consulted with company maintenance and elected to carry out a precautionary engine shutdown. Appropriate checklists were completed en route to Slave Lake, AB (CYZH) where a one engine inoperative landing was carried out without incident. Company maintenance replaced the # 2 engine tach-generator which functionally tested serviceable.

A14Q0099: Le 22 juin 2014, le CL-415 immatriculé C-GQBD du Service Aérien Gouvernemental du Québec, effectuait une envolée de lutte aux incendies de forêt dans la région de Shefferville, Québec avec 2 membres d'équipage. Lors d'un écopage, l'équipage a entendu un bruit sourd et a décidé de remonter les écopes et de se poser à l'aéroport de Shefferville (CYKL). Après évaluation des dommages à la quille, jugés mineurs, l'avion est retourné à sa base de Sept-Îles où une évaluation plus approfondie a été effectuée. L'avion a ensuite été acheminé vers la base de Québec (CYQB) où des réparations ont été effectuées afin de remettre l'appareil en service.Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

A14P0125:  The Conair Convair (580),C-FFKF, flight FGD444 departed Kamloops on a fire suppression mission. On climb-out the right engine (Allison 501D13H) failed. The engine was secured and an emergency was declared with Kamloops radio. The aircraft  proceeded to the Kamloops abort zone and jettisoned the load before returning for an uneventful landing.It was determined there was a bearing failure in the turbine section.  An SDR will be filed with Transport Canada.

A14P0131:  The Alpine Helicopters Bell 212 C-FAHB was struck by lightning while engaged in water bucketing activities on Fire 20173 in B.C. M/R rotor blade damage was evident.Mandatory Inspections include overhaul of the Transmission, M/R hub, mast, tail rotor and gearboxes.  Damage also occurred to numerous avionics components and engine instruments.  The helicopter was trailered to the company's maintainence facility for repair.

A14W0131: The United States registered Piper PA-14, N4279H, was on a flight from Red Deer, AB to Grande Prairie, AB with a final destination in Alaska. The flight encountered heavy smoke from forest fires and slowed up due to poor visibility. Near Grande Prairie the pilot reported running out of fuel and was heading for a road for a forced landing. The flight ended on an unoccupied baseball diamond. There was substantial damage to the aircraft; no injuries to the 2 occupants and no post-crash fire.

An Air Tractor AT-802A on amphibious floats (registration C-GXNX, serial number AT-802A-0530), operating as Tanker 685, was carrying out wildfire management operations during daylight near Chantslar Lake, British Columbia. Three similar aircraft were working as a group with Tanker 685, which was second in line on a touch-and-go to scoop water from Chantslar Lake. Upon liftoff, control was lost and the aircraft’s right wing struck the water. The aircraft water-looped, and the floats and their support structure separated from the fuselage. The aircraft remained upright and slowly sank. The pilot received minor injuries, egressed from the cockpit, and inflated the personal flotation device being worn. The third aircraft in the formation jettisoned its hopper load as it continued its takeoff and remained in the circuit. The fourth aircraft jettisoned its hopper load, rejected its takeoff and taxied to pick up the accident pilot. There was sufficient impact force to activate the on-board 406-megahertz emergency locator transmitter, but the search-and-rescue satellite system did not detect a signal from the emergency locator transmitter until the wreckage was being recovered 6 days later.

A14W0141: The Federal Express Boeing 777F28 Freighter, N880FD, was operating as flight FDX195 from Memphis, TN (KMEM) to Anchorage, AK (PANC). En route to PANC, the flight crew received a cabin fire indication. The flight crew declared an emergency with ATC and diverted to Whitehorse, YT (CYXY). FDX195 landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. ARFF crews inspected the aircraft and determined no fire present. Update 23 September 2014: Main deck fire suppression penetrator module (part number VAFSS7500-501) at position 2R replaced.

After departing the Abbotsford (CYXX) control zone, the flight crew of the Conair Group Convair CVLT 580 operating VFR as flight FGD444 requested flight following from CYXX Tower. The CYXX Tower Controller issued the incorrect en route frequency for flight following. About 10NM east of CYXX, FGD444 entered Class C airspace prior to approval, and came into conflict with an RCMP Pilatus PC12 (C-GMPA) operating an IFR flight inbound to Boundary Bay (CZBB). The aircraft were opposite direction at 4.6 NM and same altitude when ATC turned C-GMPA. They passed within 2.5 NM and 500 feet.

Le CL415, évoluant sous l'indicatif de vol QUE241, immatriculé C-GQBC, opéré par le Service Aérien du Gouvernement du Québec, effectuait une envolée dans la région de Québec. Lors de l'atterrissage sur la piste 24, les freins du côté droit ont surchauffés et de la fumée a été aperçue par le contrôleur de la tour. Par mesure de précaution, les Services d'urgence ont été avisés et déployés. L'appareil a été escorté jusqu'aux installations du Service Aérien. Aucun dommage n'a été découvert suite à l'inspection par l'équipe de maintenance.

The pilot of the Cessna 337 H (C-FSIY), operated by Discovery Air Fire Services, was unable to get the landing gear down indication inbound to Sudbury, ON (CYSB). The aircraft conducted a fly by and the gear was visually confirmed extended; however, all landing gear doors appeared to be open. The pilot requested emergency services on standby and the aircraft landed without incident.

The Lockheed Electra (L188C), C-FLXT, operated by Airspray (1967) Ltd., was returning to Prince George, BC after dispensing a load of retardant. During completion of the climb-out checklist from the fire zone, the engine oil quantity for the #4 engine (Allison 501-D13) was observed to have lost 6 out of 8 gallons since completion of the pre-bombing checklist. The crew completed a precautionary engine shut down and completed the planned return to Prince George. Maintenance action identified a broken wire at the oil quantity transmitter which produced a false indication.

operation: AIR TRANSPORT; FIRE FIGHTING / FIRE MANAGEMENT
Summary: The McMurray Aviation Cessna C-208 (C-FXCL) was conducting a VFR flight from Fort Chipewyan, AB (CYPY) to Fort McMurray, AB (CYMM).  C-FXCL was cruising at 3500 feet AGL.  A Lakeshore Helicopters Ltd. Airbus Helicopters AS-350-B3 (C-GLHV) was on a VFR flight from Fort McMurray, AB (CYMM) to Fort Chipewyan, AB (CYPY) to conduct smoke watch operations. C-GLHV was in cruise flight at 3000 feet AGL due to smog over the oil sands area and broadcast three position reports on the North Oil Sands ATF.  C-GLHV acquired visual contact with C-FXCL at a distance of approximately 2 nm and began to descend to 2500 feet AGL.  Visual contact was maintained with C-FXCL while passing overhead of C-GLHV. With C-FXCL maintaining flight at 3500 feet AGL and C-GLHV descending to 2500 feet AGL, a separation of 1000 feet was achieved. C-FXCL received an ACAS warning and responded.  Both aircraft were on the North Oil Sands ATF.

The Sequoia Helicopters Ltd. Bell 212 (C-GTHK), departed Fox Creek, AB (CED4) to conduct fire suppression operations on a wildfire located 8 nm north west of the town of Lodgepole, AB. While in the water bucketing circuit, as the pilot started to lift the bucket from the water source, he felt what seemed like a rapid succession of compressor stalls. The pilot noticed the # 1 Engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6T-3B) N1 (Gas Producer Speed) decreasing and engine inlet turbine temperature increasing. The pilot declared Mayday and made a precautionary landing at a nearby lease site.  The water bucket and long line were released on short final to the lease site and an uneventful landing was made.  After engine shutdown the pilot activated the emergency switch on the Skytrac system.  The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was uninjured.  The ELT was not activated. Ejected engine parts damaged the turbine casing, exhaust ducting and tail rotor blades.Update: 20 May 2015, Company maintenance has determined that the # 1 Engine Power Turbine wheel failed.

The Airspray (1967) Ltd. Lockheed 188A, C-GZVM, was dispatched to a fire in the vicinity of Fox Lake, AB. Having dropped the load at the fire and climbing out for the return to Fort McMurray, AB (CYMM), it was noticed that the oil quantity of the #2 engine (Allison 501-D13) had decreased from the amount noted on departure. The oil quantities were closely monitored for 10-20 minutes and it was determined that the #2 engine oil quantity was very slowly decreasing. At this point, the election was made to do a precautionary shutdown of the #2 engine. Maintenance suspected an issue with the #2 engine turbine labyrinth seal.

The Conair amphibious float-equipped Air Tractor AT-802A Fire Boss, C-FDHV, serial number 802A-0348, was operating as Tanker 692 in support of wildfire management operations 25 nautical miles northwest of Cold Lake, Alberta. Tanker 692 was the last in a formation of 4 AT-802A Fire Boss aircraft followed by 2 CL 215T aircraft being operated by Conair Group Inc. Tanker 692 had completed 2 drops on the fire, from west to east, with a turnout to the north. When exiting its third drop, Tanker 692 encountered severe turbulence and then pitched to a nose-up attitude. The aircraft climbed to approximately 400–500 feet above ground level, where it rolled to the left and entered a nose-down attitude. It struck the ground right-wing low and close to nose-level at 1630 Mountain Daylight Time. The pilot was fatally injured as a result of non-survivable impact forces. There was no post-impact fire.

The Transwest Air Ltd. Bell 205A-1, C-FYHD, was conducting bucketing operations in support of forest fire suppression activity west of Trout Lake, AB. While maneuvering to pick up a load of water, the descent rate of the helicopter began to increase. The pilot lowered the nose to transit forward but did not release the longline before it pulled tight as the bucket was already in the water. As the longline detached from the belly of the helicopter, the helicopter nosed up and down and spun around. The pilot regained control and set down on the Trout Lake, AB (CFB4) airstrip to assess the damage. Damage was limited to aircraft skins immediately around the belly hook.

The Skyline Helicopters Bell BH212, C-GSLZ, was conducting water bucket operations on a forest fire 42 nm NE of Lac La Biche, AB (CYLB). While en route for a water drop, the bucket and long line released uncommanded from the aircraft. There were no injuries or damage related to the load drop; however, the bucket itself was destroyed. The manual and electric release systems were normal and functional prior to flight. After the event, maintenance found that there was no free play in the manual release cable due to a worn barrel on the manual release return spring mounting bracket (Item 52: P/N 204-070-999-001). A SDR has been filed with Transport Canada.

The Helicopter Transport Services Bell 204B, registration C-FDZE, was conducting fire suppression operations at Denare Beach, Saskatchewan. While in transit to fill the bucket with water, the bucket unintentionally released. The bucket was lost, dropped in approximately 30 feet of water and will be recovered.

The Yellowhead Helicopters Ltd. Bell 212 (C-FYHT), departed Fox Lake, AB (CEC3) to conduct fire suppression operations on a wildfire located 22 nm SE of CEC3. During the initial climb away from CEC3, C-FYHT experienced an uncommanded pitch excursion nose down and to the right while approximately 1000 feet agl.  The pilot leveled the helicopter but continued sinking. During this time, the pilot observed, with an externally mounted mirror, that the water bucket (attached to 120 foot longline) was rising behind the helicopter.  The pilot then heard 2 loud bangs in quick succession when the tail rotor severed the longline.   The pilot did not experience any loss of control and returned to CEC3 without further incident. Minor damage was noted on the tail rotor blades.  The pilot was the sole occupant onboard and was uninjured.

The Airspray Airtankers Lockheed 188A, C-FDTH, was operating 60 nm NE of Dawson City, YT. On an overshoot from a water bomber run with 80% of the load remaining, the #2 engine (Allison 501-D13) lost power. Clear of terrain and climbing on the overshoot, the crew completed the engine failure drill and performed the applicable abnormal checklist. Actions taken included aborting the remaining retardant load and returning to base at Dawson City.

The Government of Saskatchewan Canadair CL-215 aircraft, registration C-FYWO, was en route to the La Ronge, Saskatchewan airport with a crew of two onboard. While in cruise, the crew noticed an excessive cylinder head temperature indication of the right engine (P&W R 2800). The crew conducted a precautionary shutdown of the right engine and continued to La Ronge where the aircraft landed safely. An inspection of the right engine revealed a fractured exhaust ear on the #2 cylinder.

The Air Spray (1967) Ltd. Aero Commander 690B, C-FMCX, was operating as flight ASB58 from Fort McMurray, AB (CYMM) to Red Deer, AB (CYQF). As soon as C-FMCX was airborne the aircraft yawed to the left. The pilot had difficulty trimming the aircraft for coordinated flight and required almost full right rudder trim to do so. During acceleration to cruise speed (accelerating through 200 KIAS) the aircraft rolled aggressively to the right achieving more than 45 degrees of bank before the pilot was able to recover with aileron and a reduction in power. A passenger in the right seat, who was a pilot with the company, assisted the pilot with rudder inputs to maintain control of the aircraft. A decision was made to return to CYMM where ARFF was on standby for the landing. It was determined that the external rudder lock had not been removed prior to flight. Damage was limited to the vertical stabilizer and rudder skins.

The Buffalo Airways Ltd. Canadair CL-215, C-GBPD, was operating as TNK291 in the vicinity of Yellowknife, NT (CYZF). TNK291 advised ATC that they were returning to CYZF with one engine shutdown. TNK291 performed an uneventful single-engine approach and landing on Runway 28. Maintenance determined that the number 17 cylinder on the number 1 engine (PRATT & WHITNEY-USA, R-2800-CA3) was cracked. The cylinder was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

The Thebacha Helicopters Ltd. Airbus Helicopters AS350-B2 (C-GXLD) was conducting forest fire fighting operations in the area of Fort Simpson, NT. Prior to landing in CYFS, the pilot maneuvered to set down the water bucket. While preparing to set down on the landing pad beside the bucket, the tail rotor blades contacted a fuel drum. The helicopter touched down shortly thereafter and remained upright. There was significant damage to the tail rotor, tail rotor gear box, tail boom, ventral fin and collateral damage to the horizontal stabilizer from tail rotor blade fragments. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was uninjured.

The Air Spray (1967) Ltd. Lockheed L188C, C-GHZI, was performing forest fire fighting operations 25 nm west of Manning, AB. During a drop on the fire, the No. 1 and No. 2 engines (Allison 501-D13) lost power. The flight crew observed the No. 1 and No. 2 engines overtemp lights illuminate and conducted the engine failure drills for the No. 1 and 2 engines. The flight crew then diverted to Manning, AB for an uneventful two engines approach and landing. The No. 1 engine exhibited signs of an overtemp event; the No. 2 engine is undergoing examination by company maintenance to determine the power loss.

The Airspray Airtankers Aero Commander 690A, C-FIIL, was on a fire fighting work near Watson Lake, YT when the left engine (Garrett TPE331-5-251K) temperature ITT climbed beyond 923 degrees Celcius while at 7000 feet in low power cruise (250 HP) and the decision was made to shut it down. All company SOPs were followed and the aircraft was flown to Watson Lake without incident.There was no indication of over temperature from engine over temp inspection. Further trouble shooting by maintenance confirms that it was a faulty ITT gauge that gave a false reading.

An Air Tractor AT-802A Fire Boss, C-GSXW, operated by Conair as Tanker 694, was conducting wildfire control operations off of Puntzi Lake, BC with one pilot on board. Tanker 694 lifted off the water with the 29th scooping load of the day. Moments after liftoff, the aircraft rolled sharply left and the left wing struck the water. The aircraft yawed left, and the floats were torn from the fuselage during the following water contact. The aircraft came to rest upright in the water but quickly sank as the uninjured pilot evacuated the single seat cockpit. The pilot was wearing a helmet, a personal floatation device and had a portable air bottle at hand. An ELT signal was not received by the SARSAT system until the aircraft was brought back to the surface 6 days later.

The Wildcat Helicopters Bell 412, C-FWTK, was water bucketing 25 NM NNE of Slave Lake, AB, in support of forest fire operations. During an approach to refill the water bucket, a loss of power and directional control was experienced. The pilot was unable to initiate an autorotation from a very low altitude and attempted a forced landing in a muskeg area. The hard landing resulted in a severed tail boom and other substantial damage. The main driveshaft forward coupling failed. The pilot sustained minor injuries and was held in hospital overnight. The operator and TSB are continuing to investigate.The forward main driveshaft coupling, part number 212-040-688-003 and the coupling boot part number 212-040-176-101 were destroyed. The investigation continues to determine reasons for the failure.

The Conair CV580, C-FKFL, was operating with two pilots on board and had landed in Kamloops (CYKA), BC.  After landing and while taxiing, the right engine (Allison 501D 13D) TIT spiked after the crew downshifted the engine.  The engine E-handle was pulled and when smoke was observed from the right engine area, the crew discharged the engine fire bottle.  Airport ARFF was deployed to the aircraft.  Subsequent maintenance inspection determined that the speed sense valve was faulty and had caused the 5th and 10th stage bleed valves to remain closed, resulting in the over temperature, with smoke resulting from unburned fuel after shut down.

A Bell B214B-1 helicopter, N281JL, operated by East West Helicopters, was carrying out bucketing operations about 15 nm south of Penticton, BC. The external load (Bambi Bucket) dropped into a pond, without being commanded, while lifting the load. The external belly hook functioned normally but was removed for load testing.

The Air Spray Ltd. Air Commander AC-690, C-GKDZ, was operating as Birddog 54, from Slave Lake, AB (CYZH) to conduct fire suppression operations. C-GKDZ broadcasted on the CYZH mandatory frequency, taxiing for Runway 28 for departure to the South West, as well as advising upon lining up on the runway. C-GKDZ made a mandatory frequency call that the aircraft was rolling on Runway 28 and departing to the SW. During this time, a Great Slave Helicopters Ltd. Bell 412, C-GMVN, departed from the firebase at Slave Lake, AB (CYZH) to conduct fire suppression operations. The firebase is located just to the north of the departure end of Runway 28. While transitioning to forward flight, C-GMVN flew west in the vicinity of the departure end of Runway 28. C-GKDZ took evasive action to the right to avoid the collision.

The Remote Helicopters Ltd. Bell 205 (C-GRHW), departed Loon River, AB (CFS6) to conduct fire suppression operations on a wildfire located 38 nm east of CFS6. Approximately one hour into the flight and after dropping a water load, C-GRHW began to return to the water pick-up point. During this time, the pilot smelled something abnormal. The pilot assessed the fire light, master caution, fuses and instruments and no abnormalities were noted. Smoke began entering the cockpit from the ceiling and hydraulic fluid was observed running down the front transmission bulkhead in the cabin. The pilot declared an emergency and released the water bucket. C-GRHW made an off field landing in a forest clearing with no additional damage. After landing, the pilot observed the master caution light to be illuminated as well as the # 2 Hydraulic system failure indication. The pilot was the sole occupant onboard. The ELT was not activated. The operator’s maintenance found a flexible hydraulic line to be broken.

Le CL-415T, immatriculé C-GQBF et exploité par le Service Aérien gouvernemental du Québec, effectuait un vol d'entraînement selon les règles de vol à vue à partir de l'aéroport de Québec/Jean-Lesage Intl (CYQB) sous l'indicatif QUE244 avec 2 pilotes à bord. Quelques minutes après le décollage, une odeur inhabituelle semblant provenir du système de climatisation a été sentie dans le cockpit.  L'équipage a mis l'interrupteur de la climatisation à "off" et l'odeur s'est progressivement dissipée. L'équipage a toutefois décidé de revenir à l'aéroport de Québec. Après l'atterrissage, l'odeur est réapparue de façon forte. De la fumée s'est ensuite manifestée dans le cockpit et l'équipage a demandé la présence des véhicules d'urgence. L'équipage a garé l'aéronef à l'écart des autres appareils et bâtiments.

After commencing a take-off roll on Runway 16 at Nanaimo, BC (CYCD), the Cessna 525 CitationJet (C-GPCT) operated by Conair Group Inc. as flight FGD115, aborted the take-off. The flight crew later advised that they had to shut the left engine down (Williams International, FJ44-1A). The pilot determined that the front spinner on the left engine cracked, failed and was embedded in the engine intake. Inspection of the engine by the operator’s maintenance and a Williams International representative determined that the damage was limited to the spinner and engine intake.

C-FZCS, an Air Spray Ltd Lockheed Electra L188 aircraft, was operating as Tanker T-487 from Red Deer, AB (CYQF) on a training flight over the Rocky Mountain House, AB (CYRM) VOR at an altitude of 10 500 feet ASL. During a stall practice exercise, as the flight crew added power upon the stall recovery maneuver, the number 2 engine (Allison 501-D13) went into an under-speed condition of 13 200 rpm (normal condition is 13 820 rpm). The flight crew actioned the SOP and performed the engine failure drill. The aircraft returned to CYQF and landed without further incident. No emergency was declared and there were no injuries.

C-FYWO, a Province of Saskatchewan (Ministry of the Environment) Canadair CL215, was operating as flight TKR214 on a local VFR test flight from La Ronge/Barber Field, SK (CYVC). The flight crew received a fire warning bell from the right hand engine (P&WC R2800) after departure. The checklist and a precautionary shutdown were completed and subsequently an electrical outage was experienced. The aircraft remained in the circuit, landed uneventfully, and was towed off the runway. Maintenance found a fault in the right engine fire detection loop system and a loose battery connector.

C-FEKF, a Conair Group Convair 580, was in the descent for landing on Runway 25 at Manning, AB (CFX4) when one of the pilots became incapacitated. As the other pilot took control of the aircraft and performed the landing, directional control was lost on the rollout. The aircraft departed the right side of the runway and travelled across a ditch, approximately 3000 feet from the threshold. The nose gear collapsed and the fuselage broke into 2 sections. There were no injuries, however the aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GHTK, a Helicopter Transport Services (Canada) Inc Bell 212 helicopter, was en route from Red Lake, ON (CYRL) to Woodland Caribou Provincial Park to conduct Bambi bucket operations in support of forest fire suppression. The helicopter was travelling at approximately 85 knots when the empty Bambi bucket became disconnected from the guarded hook. The lower section of the Bambi bucket was damaged upon impact with the ground.

The Airspan Helicopters Bell 212, C-GLYO, was conducting fire suppression operations from Worsley, AB (CFY7/Abandoned). C-GLYO was en route to a fire approximately 25 nautical miles north west of CFY7 with a longline and slung load (Bambi Bucket) when moderate turbulence was experienced and the slung load was unintentionally released. The flight was conducted over remote/uninhabited terrain. There were no injuries or damage to the aircraft.

C-GSLZ, a Skyline Helicopters Bell 212 helicopter, was conducting water bucketing operations in the vicinity of Gordon Lake, AB (CFW2). During a water drop, the pilot was unable to release the water load. A tail pylon rock started to develop, so the water bucket was jettisoned as a precaution. There were no injuries to anyone and the bucket was recovered the next day. It is suspected that the electrical connection to the bucket had come loose. All systems tested serviceable after the incident.

C-GZVM, a Lockheed L-188A Electra operated by Air Spray (1967) Ltd, was operating as flight ASB485 to a forest fire in the vicinity of High Level, AB (CYOJ). While transiting to the fire, the crew noticed that the TIT, Fuel Flow and HP indications on the number 4 engine (Allison 501-D13) would not change, regardless of power lever position. The crew also tried to adjust the TD system, prop sync and phase, however nothing worked. The crew decided to jettison the load and returned to CYOJ. The Engine Failure checklist was carried out and a precautionary shutdown of the number 4 engine was executed. The aircraft landed at CYOJ without further incident.

C-GZVM, a Lockheed L-188A Electra operated by Air Spray (1967) Ltd, was operating as ASB485 to a fire approximately 60 nautical miles west of Loon River, AB (CFS6). After a bombing run, the flight crew observed that the Number 4 engine (Allison 501-D13) hung at 200HP and 600 TIT. When power was applied, the RPM decreased. The flight crew shut the Number 4 engine down as per SOPs and diverted to High Level, AB (CYOJ) for an uneventful 3 engine approach and landing. The operator’s maintenance trouble shooting in ongoing; see A16W0073 for similar event.

C-FIJX, the Buffalo Airways Ltd. Lockheed L-188C, was conducting fire suppression operations 74 nm NE of Fort Smith, NT (CYSM). While conducting a bombing run FIJX experienced a loss of power in the # 1 and #4 engines (Allison 501-D13). The flight crew actioned the SOP and performed the engine failure drill for both the #1 and #4 engines. The aircraft returned to CYSM and landed uneventfully. No emergency was declared and there were no injuries. The power section of engine # 1 experienced a compressor stall and engine #4 had decoupled.

C-GQBK, un CL415 exploité par Service aérien gouvernemental a décollé de Sept-Îles dans le cadre d'une mission de feu au nord de Sept-Îles (Québec). Après la phase d’écopage d’eau, sur la montée,  l’aéronef est entré en collision avec un voilier de canards. Un des canards a heurté le refroidisseur d’huile du moteur gauche et est resté coincé en place. Lors du retour à Sept-Îles, la pression d’huile du moteur de gauche (P & W CAN PW123AF) s’est mise à baisser et la température d’huile a monté suivi de l'illumination du voyant Master Caution Warning. L’équipage a effectué la procédure d’arrêt et de mise en drapeau du moteur et a déclaré une urgence. L’approche et l’atterrissage se sont déroulés sans autres incidents. Une inspection de l’appareil n’a révélé aucun autre dommage à l’exception du refroidisseur d’huile. Le refroidisseur d’huile du moteur de gauche a été remplacé et l’avion fut remis en service.

C-FIJX, a Lockheed 188C Electra aircraft operated by Buffalo Airways Ltd, was conducting forest fire suppression operations from Hay River/Merlyn Carter, NT (CYHY). During a bombing run, the flight crew observed the number 1 propeller RPM drop below the lower limit. A precautionary shutdown of the number 1 engine (Allison 501-D13) was carried out in accordance with the L-0188 Standard Operating Procedures. The retardant load was jettisoned and a 3 engine landing was carried out in CYHY without further incident.

C-FZTK, a Bell 205A-1 helicopter operated by Churchill Falls (Labrador) Corporation Ltd, was conducting a local water bucketing training flight from Churchill Falls, NL (CZUM) with 2 crew members on board. The crew was conducting water drops operation about 0.5 nautical mile North East of CZUM when, on the fifth drop, the water bucket was unintentionally released. The damaged water bucket was located and retrieved. The aircraft was not damaged. The incident has been entered into the operator’s safety management system for investigation and corrective action.

C-FFKF, a Convair 340-31 operated by Conair, was conducting a post-maintenance test flight and had departed Kelowna, BC (CYLW) for a local VFR flight with 2 pilots and 1 maintenance engineer on board.  During the course of the flight, the smell of smoke became evident on the flight deck. The crew actioned the emergency checklist and the aircraft returned to CYLW for an uneventful landing. A post-flight maintenance investigation found evidence of burnt paper wrapping on a phase adapter of the flight instruments power supply on the first officer’s side. A service difficulty report has been filed by the operator.

C-GYHQ, a Yellowhead Helicopter Bell 212 aircraft, was en route to Lower Fishing Lake, SK in support of local forest fire suppression. While flying back to the water source at 80 knots to reload, the pilot felt the empty water bucket release from the cargo hook. Maintenance personnel found the manual release cable was set at 70% travel. The cable was adjusted to 90% travel and the helicopter was returned to service.

C-GXNY, an Air Tractor AT-802A Fireboss amphibian aircraft operated by the Conair Group Inc, was carrying out wildfire suppression work near the west side of Lake Okanagan, west of Kelowna, BC. On the climb-out following a scoop of water, the pilot determined that the engine (PT6A-67AG) was not performing normally. The power was reduced, the load was dumped and a precautionary landing back on the lake was carried out. The pilot shut the engine down and the aircraft was towed to a dock. Follow-up work by the operator and the engine manufacturer determined that the propeller control lever was set to a cruise RPM setting and had not been advanced to the full RPM position in accordance with the approach checklist for the scooping run, take-off and climb-out.

C-FYFN, an Air Tractor AT-802A on wheels operated by the Conair Group Inc as flight FGD696, departed Castlegar/West Kootenay Regional, BC (CYCG) with a load of fire retardant. As the flight leveled off at 6 500 feet ASL, the pilot noted that engine (PT6A-67F) parameters were significantly higher than normal and the engine was not responding to power lever inputs. Since the airspeed was increasing rapidly and the engine could not be controlled, the pilot performed an intentional in-flight engine shut down and dumped the load. The flight turned back towards CYCG and an emergency was declared. However, since a suitable landing site could not immediately be found during the glide, the pilot restarted the engine temporarily in order to reach the airport. The flight glided and landed on Runway 33 at CYCG and was towed off the runway. There were no injuries or fire.

N114HQ, an Embraer 170-200LR aircraft operated by Republic Airlines, was conducting flight RPA4496 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Philadelphia Intl, PA (KPHL). During the climb after takeoff from CYYZ, the flight crew declared an emergency due to the forward cargo compartment fire suppression system failure. The aircraft returned to CYYZ and landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance placed the FWD Cargo Fire EXT on MEL 26-23-00-1 and eventually replaced the forward compartment fire bottle. An operational check was performed and no further faults were found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GKFO, a Convair 340/580 Air Tanker aircraft operated by Conair Group, departed from Abbotsford, BC (CYXX) for an IFR training flight. As the flight crew was holding at the Whatcom VOR, WA (HUH), a loss of hydraulic pressure occurred. The flight crew completed the appropriate checklist, declared an emergency and returned to CYXX. The landing gear was manually extended and the flight crew performed a flapless landing without further event. The aircraft stopped on the runway and required to be towed. The operator’s maintenance discovered that the landing gear selector valve in the left main landing gear bay had failed.

C-GHZI, a Lockheed L188C aircraft operated by Airspray (1967), was conducting a training flight near Ft. McMurray, AB (CYMM). Shortly after a training water drop, the number 1 propeller over sped to the pitch lock (14 530 rpm). The flight crew shut down the number 1 engine (Allison 501-D13), requested emergency services on standby at CYMM and completed a three engine approach and landing without further event.

C-GMFZ, a Bombardier CL-215-6B11 (CL-415) aircraft operated by the Province of Manitoba, was carrying out fire suppression operations near Red Sucker Lake, MB (CYRS). Smoke was present in the area and while turning onto final for a water drop, C-GMFZ collided with a loon. The flight crew noticed a dent in the right outboard leading edge wing just outside the propeller arc. The flight crew dropped the water load and advised the birddog that they would be returning to Thompson, MB (CYTH) where they landed without further event. The operator's maintenance confirmed the bird strike as there was minor damage to the leading edge. The aircraft was removed from service pending repairs.

operation: AIR TRANSPORT; FIRE FIGHTING / FIRE MANAGEMENT
Summary: C-GTJX, a SAAB 340B aircraft operated by Transwest Air, was conducting flight TW103 from La Ronge (Barber Field), SK (CYVC) to Prince Albert (Glass Field), SK (CYPA). Prior to taxing for departure on Runway 18 at CYVC, the flight crew of TW103 was aware of the traffic in the area. Conflicting traffic was C-GIOG, a Cessna 337G aircraft operated by Discovery Air Fire Services that was 15 nautical miles South West of CYVC. The flight crew of C-GIOG had informed through the MF frequency that they were going to enter a left downwind for Runway 18. The radio operator advised the flight crew of C-GIOG of the departing TW103 and asked C-GIOG to stay west of the departure path for Runway 18. During the initial climb, the flight crew of TW103 received a TCAS Resolution Advisory (RA) to initiate a climb. The flight crew complied with the RA and advised ATC of the deviation. The captain had visual contact with a Cessna 337 reportedly passing directly under TW103.

C-GBOW, a Canadair CL215-1A10 aircraft operated by the Province of Manitoba and engaged in fire suppression was commencing a take-off from The Pas, MB (CYQD). The engines had been idling in a rich condition and as the throttles were advanced the left engine (Pratt & Whitney R-2800 CA3) lost power. The auto-feather system activated and feathered the propeller. The flight crew rejected the take-off and taxied the aircraft back to the apron. A high power run-up was performed uneventfully, a successful flight completed and maintenance then returned the aircraft back to service.

C-GSLZ, a Bell 212 aircraft operated by Skyline Helicopters, was conducting water bucketing operations in support of forest fire fighting activities near Williams Lake, BC (CYWL). During the flight, the pilot noted that the aircraft flew into unsettled air. In order to gain airspeed and climb safely away from the terrain, the pilot elected to release the long line and water bucket. The pilot returned to CYWL without further incident.

C-GJHB, a Eurocopter EC-130 B4 helicopter operated by J.B. Air, was conducting water bucket operations on a forest fire 23 nautical miles South West of Williams Lake, BC (CYWL). As the aircraft was lifting off from a small pond with a full bucket of water, it began yawing to the left. The pilot attempted to slow the yawing motion, however was unable to regain control. The helicopter completed 2 full turns about its vertical axis before colliding with the surface of the water. The aircraft remained upright and nearby forestry personnel were able to rescue the pilot. The pilot sustained serious injuries.

C-GCCD, a Bell 412 aircraft operated by Summit Helicopters, was conducting forest fire suppression near Adams Lake, BC. During cruise flight, the long line detached from the belly of the aircraft without the pilot’s input. The line fell approximately 100 feet and was later recovered. There were no injuries and there was no damage to any equipment on the ground. An inspection of the cargo hook system was carried out and the long line was removed for inspection. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FDZT, a privately operated Cessna 180J aircraft, was conducting a VFR flight from High Level, AB (CYOJ) to Edmonton/Villeneuve, AB (CZVL). During cruise flight, the pilot experienced reduced visibility from forest fire smoke and elected to divert to Slave Lake, AB (CYZH). The pilot conducted an approach to Runway 10, however flared too high and the aircraft descended at a high rate toward the runway. The aircraft landed hard, bounced and subsequently settled down with the right wing tip and right horizontal stabilizer contacting the runway surface. The aircraft continued the landing roll and exited the runway with no further issues. The pilot, sole occupant, was uninjured. The ELT was not activated.

C-FNWB, a Bell 412 aircraft operated by Aurora Helicopters, was conducting fire suppression activities approximately 21 nautical miles South West of Nazko, BC. During the approach to the water source to refill the water bucket, the pilot noticed that the longline and bucket were no longer attached to the aircraft. The pilot returned to Quesnel, BC (CYQZ) to facilitate the inspection of the cargo restraint system.

C-GSCD, un appareil de type Cessna R182 exploité par Grondair Aviation, effectuait un vol de patrouille de feu selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de Baie-Comeau, QC (CYBC) avec seul un pilote à bord. De retour pour l’atterrissage sur la piste 28 à CYBC, l’appareil s’est posé sur le ventre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé, mais l’appareil a subi des dommages au fuselage et à l’hélice.

C-GZVM, a Lockheed 188A Electra aircraft operated by Air Spray (1967), was conducting flight Tanker 485 in the vicinity of Fort McMurray, AB (CYMM). During the flight, the flight crew observed that the number 1 propeller was overspeeding. The overspeed checklist was consulted, the number 1 engine (Allison 501-D13) was shut down and the load of retardant was jettisoned. The flight crew declared an emergency and performed an uneventful three engine approach and landing at CYMM.

C-GSPG, a Beech 95-B55 aircraft operated by the Northern Air Operations as flight BD144, was conducting an initial attack on a forest fire North of Prince Albert, SK with the pilot and one crew member on board. While in the manoeuver, the left engine (Teledyne Continental IO-470-L) began to run rough and loose power. The pilot decided to shut the engine down and diverted the aircraft to Prince Albert (Glass Field), SK (CYPA). An emergency was declared and the aircraft landed without further event.

C-GCEU, a Beech B300 King Air aircraft operated by DIS Aviation, was conducting a flight under IFR from Fairmont Hot Springs, BC (CYCZ) to Kelowna, BC (CYLW) at 10 000 feet ASL. C-FKFB, a Convair 580 aircraft operated by Conair Group, was conducting flight FGD447 under VFR from Penticton, BC (CYYF) to the northeast for the purpose of aerial forest fire suppression activities.
