The left mainwheel tire was found deflated due to a shredded patch in the center of the tread. The tire came off its wheel bead, and allowed the wheel rim to cause minor gouging damage to the chip seal runway surface. A small amount of fuel vented onto the runway surface. The landing conditions for runway were described as a light, right crosswind.

C-GZGK, a Bell 205A-1 operated by Guardian Helicopters Inc., was conducting a flight from La Ronge (CJX3) SK. to the north end of Lake Besnard SK. to drop off a forest firefighting crew. C-GZGK landed at Pad 9, located on the shore of Lake Besnard. The fire crew departed the running helicopter and were positioned at the 11 o'clock and 2 o'clock positions. Prior to departure, the doors were closed and secured, basket was closed, and pre-takeoff checks were completed. The pilot lifted the helicopter up into hover flight and started to slowly back the helicopter away from Pad 9. The helicopter tail rotor struck the water as the helicopter was backing up. A loud bang was heard coming from the rear of the helicopter followed by a nose pitch-up, an increase in the sound of the engine and main rotor rpm, and the helicopter started to spin to the right. The pilot closed the throttle and performed the procedure for a tail rotor failure. The helicopter landed upright close to the shore near Pad 9. The pilot shutdown the helicopter and exited. There were no injuries. The ELT did not activate.

C-GCMD, a Yellowhead Helicopters Limited Airbus Helicopters AS350-B2 (AStar) helicopter was conducting fire management operations with only the pilot on board. During drip torch operations, a weld failed on the suspended heli-torch and a piece of it and the associated fuel barrel fell into a previously burnt area. The equipment fell from a height of about 300 feet above ground. There were no injuries or damage to the helicopter.The fuel barrel and the part of the heli-torch were recovered.

N744CK, a cargo-configured Boeing 747-400 operated by Kalitta Air, was conducting flight CKS636 from Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky Intl (KCVG), USA to Anchorage/Ted Stevens Intl (PANC), USA. While enroute, the flight crew received multiple status messages for Cargo FWD 1 and 2, fire Protection loops A and B.  Subsequently, the EICAS (Engine Indicating and Crew Alerting System) displayed FIRE CARGO FWD warning message, as well as a Master Warning message, and the audible fire bell. The crew completed the cargo fire procedures and discharged the fire suppression system into the forward cargo compartment.  The crew then declared an emergency with Winnipeg Center and initially turned toward Cold Lake/Group Captain R.W. McNair (CYOD), AB when the aircraft was approximately 25 NM south-southwest of Flin Flon, MB. Winnipeg Center suggested to the crew that Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE) was closer, and the crew agreed that was a better option.  The crew proceeded towards CYXE and jettisoned fuel in order to decrease the aircraft weight to the maximum landing weight.  The aircraft landed safely at CYXE. Airport Emergency Services then approached the aircraft and scanned for heat sources with a thermal detector. No heat sources were detected, and the crew and Airport Emergency Services agreed it was safe to taxi the aircraft to a parking area. Once the crew was safely off the aircraft, the forward cargo compartment was opened. The discharge of the fire suppression was confirmed, and no damage to aircraft was noticed. The operator’s maintenance later determined that the fire indication was due to a fault in the fire detection system as they found evidence of AFOLTS cards shorted due to water damage. The cards were replaced, a thorough check of the system was carried out, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FGKJ, a cargo-configured Boeing 757-200 operated by CargoJet Airways Ltd., departed Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB with a destination of Montreal/Mirabel Intl (CYMX), QC. Approximately 45 minutes after takeoff, the crew was alerted to a fire indication on the left engine (Rolls-Royce RB211-535E4-37). The crew carried out an in-flight shutdown of the left engine, declared an emergency, and, upon consulting company operations, elected to return to CYWG. The crew did not deploy the fire suppression system as the fire indication cleared when the engine was idled down during the shutdown procedure. The aircraft landed without further issues. The operator’s maintenance inspected the aircraft and a defect in the fire detection system is suspected. Troubleshooting and maintenance is being performed with company and engine manufacturer resources.

C-FRTW, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 (Dreamliner) was conducting flight AC64 from Incheon International (RKSI), Seoul, Republic of Korea, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 12 crew and 300 passengers on board. After landing in CYVR, with the aircraft at the gate and the passengers deplaning, the ground crew noticed the left main gear showing smoke with a small fire present. The crew was advised and a rapid deplanement was conducted for the remaining passengers. An aircraft rescue and firefighting crew attended the scene to monitor the situation. No retardant was used, and the smoke and fire extinguished on its own.Maintenance conducted an inspection and replaced the No. 5 wheel assembly and the No. 5 brake assembly. Both assemblies that were removed have been sent for further inspection.

C-GZON, an Air Spray (1967) Ltd. Aero Commander 690 was conducting a training flight, as flight ASB055, out of Red Deer (CYQF), AB with 2 flight crew on board.  The aircraft started take-off roll from Runway 17. At approximately 60 knots the nosewheel began to shimmy and the aircraft veered towards the left side of the runway. The flight crew aborted the take off and tried to keep the aircraft on the centerline. The aircraft continued to the left and exited the runway. The aircraft came to a stop in a drainage ditch. The nose gear and left main gear collapsed and both propellers were damaged.  The flight crew were not injured and egressed from the aircraft on their own.

C-GZCF, a Lockheed L-188C Electra, operated by Air Spray 1967 Ltd. was conducting forest fire fighting operations from the Fort McMurray, AB airport (CYMM). Shortly after departure, the flight crew received a #2 engine fire indication. The flight crew ran the appropriate check list, and shut down the #2 engine (Allison 501-D13). A PAN PAN was declared with ATC, and the aircraft returned to CYMM for an uneventful landing with aircraft rescue and fire fighting (ARFF) on standby.Subsequent investigation by maintenance determined that the #2 engine fire indication was a fault with the fire indication system, and not an actual engine fire. Repairs to the fire indication system were completed, and the aircraft was returned to service.

On 04 May 2023, a Campbell Helicopters Ltd. Bell 212 helicopter was conducting water bucketing operations in support of forest fire suppression services in the vicinity of Utikuma Lake, Alberta (approximately 160 nautical miles north-northwest of Edmonton, Alberta). Onboard was the pilot. While transiting back to the water source, after the 9th water delivery, the long line and water bucket inadvertently released over a heavily wooded, non-populated area. The aircraft returned to its operating base.Maintenance action: Post-occurrence maintenance determined that an electrical short in the arming switch led to the release of the long line and water bucket. The switch, relay, and cargo hook were replaced.

C-FAVX, a Range Helicopters Inc. Airbus Helicopters AS350-B2, was returning to the Edson airport (CYET), AB, from a staging area supporting firefighting operations to the east of Edson, AB. On approach to CYET the pilot elected to expedite his arrival routing due to incoming fixed wing air traffic. On the final approach to landing, the helicopter entered a descent that resulted in a hard landing and roll-over. The pilot survived with minor injuries; the helicopter was substantially damaged. Post impact, the engine continued to run and was subsequently shut down. The ELT activated; there was no post-impact fire.

On 13 May 2023, a Conair Group Inc De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400AT air tanker (registration C-FFQG), operating as FGD542, departed the Grande Prairie Airport (CYQU), Alberta to conduct aerial firefighting operations in the local area; on board were 2 crew members. At approximately 1445 mountain daylight time (MDT), while preparing to drop water on a fire, the crew noticed that the #2 hydraulic quantity was below normal and just above the minimum for dispatch. A few minutes later, the quantity reduced below the minimum. The crew jettisoned the retardant load in the fire area and returned to CYQU. During the transit to CYQU, the crew lowered the landing gear and completed the appropriate emergency checklist procedure. As the crew completed the checklist, the associated #2 hydraulic CAUTION and ADVISORY lights illuminated. Upon initial contact with the CYQU flight service station specialist, the crew declared a "PAN PAN" emergency. The aircraft landed at 1453 MDT on Runway 30 without further incident and then towed off the runway.Maintenance actions: Maintenance personnel found a leaking hydraulic line connected to the right hand main gear "up" actuator. The line was replaced and the fluid level replenished. Additional checks were completed with no faults found and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GSKQ, a Convair CV580 aircraft operated by the Saskatchewan Public Safety Agency, was operating a fire suppression flight from Prince Albert/Glass Field (CYPA), SK to a fire in the Buffalo Narrows, SK area. After takeoff from CYPA, the crew noticed that the right propeller (Hamilton Standard 55H60-77) was in a pitch-lock condition. The crew conducted an intentional engine shutdown of the right engine and returned to CYPA for an uneventful single-engine landing. There were no injuries, nor any damage to the aircraft.The operator's maintenance reported that the right propeller controller failed and will be replaced prior to the aircraft returning to service.

In the days leading up to the day of the occurrence, the pilot of C-FKMX, an Aerospatiale AS350B3 had been conducting long line forest fire fighting operations in support of Wildfire 017 located approximately 6 nm NW of Valleyview, Alberta (CEL5) in co-ordination with C-FCCK, a Bell Helicopters model 412 operated by Summit Helicopters Ltd. On the day of the occurrence, at approximately 1234 MDT, C-FKMX had been dispatched to conduct long line bucketing operations in continued support of Wildfire 017 on the east side of Sturgeon Lake, Alberta (Sandy Bay). C-FCCK, had also been dispatched to conduct bucketing operations in support of Wildfire 017 approximately 3.5 nm SE of C-FKMX's location. In addition, C-FALI, a Bell Helicopters model 212 operated by Alpine Helicopters, was called in to assist C-FCCK in working the eastern flank of the fire line.After approximately 8-9 buckets drops in the Sandy Bay area, C-FKMX was repurposed to join C-FCCK, and C-FALI in firefighting operations on the eastern edge of the fire. Enroute to the new location, C-FKMX refilled the bucket and proceeded southeast to engage in operations. As C-FKMX approached the new area of operations; the flight crew of the three helicopters engaged in firefighting operations were all communicating on the same frequency. As C-FKMX approached the drop area from the northwest, visual contact was made with C-FALI, while communicating on the radio and broadcasting current position and intentions and trying to visually acquire the location of C-FCCK. C-FCCK responded to the radio call, but portions of the radio calls between the two pilots were not clearly understood. The pilot of C-FKMX believed that C-FCCK was clear of the immediate area, and the pilot of C-FCCK was not aware that C-FKMX was immediately joining the firefighting efforts at their location. The pilots of both C-FKMX and C-FCCK both unknowingly observed the same hotspot in the area and had elected to drop their water on it at almost the same time. Due to the pilots' seating position in each helicopter (right seat in C-FKMX, and left seat in C-FCCK) and the relative relationship of the two helicopters to each other in flight, the pilots of both helicopters did not visually acquire the other. In the process of lining up to deploy the water on the location, C-FCCK which was slightly below C-FKMX, made contact with, and severed the long line of C-FKMX approximately 28 feet below the helicopter's fuselage. The majority of the longline and bucket assembly impacted terrain in a non-populated area and both helicopters continued to fly.Departing the immediate area, the pilot of C-FKMX initiated a crab to keep the remaining portion of the severed long line from entangling the tail rotor and found a clearing to land in to complete a preliminary inspection of the helicopter. No damage was found, and the remaining portion of the long line was removed and placed in the cabin. C-FKMX repositioned to CEL5 to refuel and then return to the Valleyview firebase.The pilot of C-FCCK was unaware that his main rotor system had severed the longline of C-FKMX believing that C-FKMX had severed its own longline. C-FCCK continued to work the fire until notified by Alberta Forestry that the helicopter had been involved in an occurrence, at which time the helicopter returned to the Valleyview firebase for an inspection by company maintenance. No damage was found, and the helicopter was returned to service.A subsequent investigation by Alberta Forestry resulted in an amendment to the circuit joining procedures for aircraft joining a previously established firefighting circuit, and clarification of procedures for aircraft moving work areas.

C-FTXK, un Canadair CL-215 exploité par le Service Aérien Gouvernemental du Québec, avec à son bord 2 membres d'équipage de conduite effectuait un vol de combat de feu de forêt selon les règles de vol à vue depuis et à destination de Roberval, QC (CYRJ). Lors du deuxième largage sur un feu situé sous une ligne de transport d'électricité à haute tension d'Hydro-Québec près du mont Wright, l'appareil a subit une perte d'altitude et les portes de largage ouvertes ont touché au câble supérieur de la ligne. L'appareil a dérouté vers l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage Int, QC (CYQB) où il a atterri sans encombre. Des marques de contact ont été observées par le personnel de maintenance. Il n'y a pas eu de blessé.

C-FQNG, a Sikorsky S-61N operated by VIH Helicopters Limited, was conducting firefighting operations with a long line and bucket approximately 25 nautical miles northwest of Fort St. John (CYXJ), BC, with 2 flight crew members on board. While returning to CYXJ in level flight with an empty bucket, the pilot (who was flying from the LH seat) released the cyclic to adjust the trim. When his hand returned to the cyclic, he inadvertently pressed the cargo release button on the cyclic. The longline and bucket where jettisoned into the forest below. The aircraft continued to CYXJ. There were no injuries to anyone on the ground and the aircraft was not damaged.The company briefed flight crews on operational mitigations to reduce the likelihood of inadvertent load release.

C-FLJO, an Air Spray (1967) Limited Lockheed 188C (Electra) was conducting fire suppression operations as flight ASB482 approximately 28 nautical miles northwest of Williams Lake Airport (CYWL), BC, with 2 pilots on board. During the return flight to CYWL, to reload fire retardant, the crew observed the No. 2 engine (Allison 501-D13) oil pressure and associated reduction gear oil pressure fluctuate. The No. 2 engine lost all oil quantity and the crew performed a precautionary shutdown. The aircraft diverted to the operator's maintenance facility at Red Deer Regional Airport (CYQF), AB, and landed without incident. Maintenance found that the oil line on the rear turbine bearing carrier was broken due to a vibration. The rear turbine and bearing carrier were replaced.

C-FIEM. an Airbus Helicopters AS 350-B3 (AStar), operated by a Yellowhead Helicopters Limited, was conducting aerial firefighting operations in the vicinity of Pink Mountain, BC, with only the pilot on board. During an attempted water drop, the pilot inadvertently pressed the cargo release button which led to the bucket and the longline being released. They both landed in an un-populated area within the confines of the fire. The bucket and longline were both eventually recovered.

C-FTNH, un Cessna 310R exploité par Exact Air inc., effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR) pour la Société de protection des forêts contre le feu (SOPFEU) au départ de l’aéroport de Roberval, Qc (CYRJ). Alors que l’aéronef effectuait l’inspection de la zone de feu située à 8 milles nautiques au nord de l’aéroport de Chicoutimi/St-Honoré, Qc (CYRC), le pilote a remarqué une indication de surchauffe de température d’huile pour le moteur gauche. Le pilote a actionné la liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et a fermé le moteur. Une fois le moteur sécurisé, le pilote a demandé l’autorisation d’atterrir à CYRC. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre et a circulé vers les installations d’Exact Air sur son propre pouvoir.  L’inspection au sol a révélé qu’un connecteur desserré dans le faisceau de câble de la jauge de température d’huile était à l’origine de l’indication de surchauffe.

C-GOSX, a Piper Aerostar PA-60-600, operated by Forest Protection Limited as BD171 was on a positioning flight from Fredericton Intl. Airport, NB (CYFC) to Yarmouth Airport, NS (CYQI) for birddog duty in forest fire operations. On approach to RWY33 at CYQI the pilot selected gear down and noted that the nose landing gear (NLG) indicator did not illuminate. The pilot executed a go around and re-entered the circuit. On the downwind leg the landing gear was cycled two more times without a change in the NLG down indication even though the reflection of the NLG in the prop spinner showed that it was extended. The NLG bulb was checked and found to be serviceable after which the pilot elected to return to CYFC.On approach to RWY 33 at CYFC the gear was lowered, and the NLG not locked indication persisted. The pilot contacted CYFC tower and requested Airport Rescue and Fire Fighting be on standby. The aircraft landed safely at 14:29 AST. Maintenace determined that the NLG not locked indication problem was due to a broken wire.

C-FFQV, a Conair Group Incorporated De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402AT air tanker, departed Abbotsford (CYXX), BC, as flight FGD547, to conduct firebombing training in the vicinity of Harrison Lake, BC with 2 crew members on board. After the fourth drop, the crew were alerted that the retardant tank doors did not close. The associated warning alarm could not be silenced and interfered with crew communication with air traffic control. The flight returned to the CYXX area and, after discussions with ground-based maintenance, the crew reset the retardant tank system which eventually silenced the tank door warning. When the crew lowered the landing gear, the gear warning horn became active and could not be silenced. The crew declared a "PAN PAN" emergency and conducted a low pass for a visual inspection by CYXX Tower controller. The controller confirmed the aircraft appeared normal and the crew landed without further incident.Maintenance personnel were unable to replicate the fault on the ground and a subsequent flight was conducted with no faults found. Maintenance and engineering have developed supplementary quick reference handbook procedures for resetting the tank door system and audio alerts. They are developing dedicated reset switches for the door and audio alert systems.

C-GERL, a Qwest Helicopters (2020) Limited Aerospatiale AS350 BA (AStar) was conducting long line firefighting operations under visual flight rules from fire G90709 to a landing site located approximately 28 nautical miles south-southeast of Fort Liard Airport (CYJF), NT, with one crewmember on board. At 1633 Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), while backing up to land on the helipad, the tail rotor of the helicopter struck a pack that had been left on the helipad. The tail rotor assembly subsequently departed the helicopter. There were no injuries. The helicopter was substantially damaged.The helicopter was recovered and was repaired in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions. It has been returned to service.

C-GIAA, an Aero Commander operated by Conair Group Incorporated, was conducting a local fire fighting flight from Smithers (CYYD), BC, with 2 crew and 1 passenger on board. During the takeoff roll, the pilot noticed some drift to the right and sensed a reduction in the acceleration rate. The throttle positions were confirmed as matched, but the right engine (Garrett TPE 331-10T-515K) power gauge was indicating 120 hp whereas the planned takeoff setting was 600 hp. The right throttle was advanced but no change in power was noted. The takeoff was aborted at 92 kts (critical engine-failure recognition speed, V1, was 95 kts) and aggressive braking was used to ensure a safe stop on the available runway remaining. After assessing the situation, the crew taxied clear of the runway. They then noted some smoke from the left main landing gear. To cool the brakes, they prolonged the taxi before parking. After parking, the brakes continued smoking and hydraulic fluid was seen running from the left main gear. Company maintenance personnel used fire extinguishers to douse the left and right main wheels. The crew requested emergency services to assist. There was no fire.After troubleshooting the engine issue, the cause of the power reduction was a failed (blocked) propeller governor reset orifice and check valve assembly. They also replaced the left and right main landing gear tires, wheels, and brakes.

C-GDAA, a Conair Group Incorporated Rockwell International Commander 690B, was conducting fire suppression operations as flight FGD136 out of Smithers (CYYD), BC, with the pilot and an air attack officer on board. While in cruise, the power of the No. 1 engine (Garrett TPE331-10T-516K) decreased to idle. Attempts to regain engine were not effective and the pilot completed an engine shutdown. A PAN PAN was declared with air traffic control and the flight returned to CYYD where it landed without further incident.Maintenance determined that the T2 temperature sensor probe had failed. The affected sensor was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service. Conair will work with the manufacturers of the engine and the T2 probe to determine the cause of the failure.

C-FOLB, an AS350-B2 operated by Helicopters Canada, was conducting VFR flight MNR718 for firefighting support from the MNR Base at Sioux Lookout, ON, to Arril Lake, ON. During the landing phase at Arril lake, the floating landing platform moved unexpectedly. The aircraft's tail rotor was struck by the platform structure. The pilot maneuvered the aircraft away from the platform and autorotated into the lake. The rotor brake was applied fully and the aircraft came to rest upright in 3 feet of water. One passenger sustained a minor injury. The ELT activated and MNR dispatch was notified immediately. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GRUV, a Valhalla Helicopters Inc. Bell 205A-1, was operating in support of forest fire fighting activities in the vicinity of Haig Lake, AB, 55 nm NE of Peace River Airport (CYPE), AB. Shortly after departure to commence bucketing operations the helicopter collided with terrain. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was fatally injured. The ELT activated; the helicopter was substantially damaged and there was no post-impact fire. The TSB Edmonton office deployed investigators to the site.

Summary: The Air Spray (1967) Ltd. Lockheed L188C, C-FLXT, was operating as ASB481 from Red Deer (CYQF), AB to Williams Lake (CYWL), BC. During the climb to cruise the flight crew observed large fluctuations on the #2 propeller (AEROPRODUCTS, A6441FN-606A S/N HC683) and a resulting pitch lock. The #2 engine (ALLISON, 501-D13 S/N CAE501265) was shut down as a precaution and the flight returned to CYQF and landed uneventfully. Maintenance Update: The #2 propeller regulator was found to be at fault. Regulator S/N R895 removed and regulator S/N R1145 installed. Ground run and pitch lock check completed with no faults found and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GVFH, a Conair Group Incorporated BAE Systems RJ85, was conducting local firefighting operations as flight FGD561 under visual flight rules from Kamloops Airport (CYKA), BC, with 2 crewmembers on board. On the return to CYKA, on approach to Runway 09, during landing gear extension, a caution message indicating low fluid level in the GREEN hydraulic system occurred. The crew observed the associated hydraulic system quantity to be one third full and elected to continue the approach. After final flap selection, the associated hydraulic system quantity and pressure indicated zero. With selection of the airbrake, and with subsequent use of systems powered by the GREEN hydraulic system, the crew reported abnormal sounds, suspected to be hydraulic pump cavitation. After landing, the crew were able to clear the runway, onto Taxiway B, where the aircraft was shut down and towed to the tanker base. A maintenance inspection determined that there was a leak in a right-hand lift spoiler selector valve. The component was replaced, hydraulic fluid was replenished, and a successful ground function test was completed. The aircraft has been returned to service.

C-GYSJ, a Central Mountain Air Ltd. de Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-102 (Dash 8) was preparing to conduct flight GLR9316, under instrument flight rules, from Port Hardy Airport (CYZT), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, with 3 crewmembers on board. At 1730 Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), while on the apron in CYZT, the crew attempted to start the aircraft auxiliary power unit (APU). The start was unsuccessful, and the APU along with the aircraft batteries were cycled off prior to attempting a second start. During the second start attempt, ground crew observed black smoke coming from the tail section of the aircraft and informed the flight crew. A flight crew member exited the aircraft to visually observe the smoke and the crew concluded that they were experiencing an APU fire. The APU fault light inside the cockpit was illuminated, but the APU fire warning light was not. Manual discharge of the APU fire bottle was accomplished, and the fire department was called. Fire crews found high temperatures in the APU compartment but determined no further extinguishing agents were required.A maintenance inspection found no signs of fire within the APU but did find evidence of an APU generator overheat, along with damage to the APU generator. The APU generator was repaired, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GBEP, a Summit Helicopters Limited Bell 412EP helicopter, was conducting long-line firefighting operations in the vicinity of fire K21633 (Bush Creek East), BC, under visual flight rules with 1 crew member on board. At 1700 Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), after departing a remote refueling point to return to the fire, a master caution light illuminated, indicating a system 1 hydraulic malfunction. Hydraulic pressure for the number 1 system indicated 0, and failure of the system was further confirmed via manipulation of the tail rotor pedals. The pilot diverted approximately 30 nautical miles southwest to the Kamloops Airport (CYKA), BC, and performed the required emergency checks. Upon arrival at the CYKA control zone, the pilot declared an emergency. The slung load was jettisoned onto the airport ramp and the helicopter landed without further incident. A maintenance investigation will be undertaken by the operator to determine the cause of the hydraulic system failure.

C-GNCS, a Buffalo Airways Ltd. Canadair CL-215 (serial 1008) was departing Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), Northwest Territories on a local fire-fighting mission. On board were 2 pilots. After lining up for departure on Runway 28, the pilots carried out the remaining pre-takeoff checklist items. During that time, the engine RPM on the left-hand engine slowly began decreasing. The reduction of engine RPM on the left-hand engine went undetected until the engine stopped due to flooding. The crew of TKR291 then taxied off the runway and back to the company hangar. The engine was restarted, and the flight was completed without further incident. There was no damage and no injuries.

C-FYWP, a Buffalo Airways Ltd. Canadair Ltd. CL215-1A10, was conducting forest fire fighting operations in the vicinity of Gordon Lake, NT, 53 NM NE of Yellowknife, NT. During a scooping run on Gordon Lake, the aircraft struck an object. The take-off was rejected and the captain water taxied to the shore to park the aircraft. A helicopter picked up the flight crew to return them to Yellowknife. Damage to the lower forward section of the hull was substantial.UPDATED 02 NOVEMBER 2023

C-GYJZ, a Jazz Aviation LP de Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), was preparing to conduct flight JZA416 under instrument flight rules from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Penticton Airport (CYYF), BC, with 4 crew members and 20 passengers on board. Prior to pushback, cabin crew reportedly detected the smell of electrical smoke. While investigating the source of the fumes, a passenger approached a cabin crew member with an external battery that showed signs of being abnormally hot. The external battery was placed inside a lithium-ion battery incident kit (LIBIK). The LIBIK containing the battery was removed from the aircraft and retrieved by fire crews for disposal of the battery inside. Prior to departure, the empty LIBIK was returned to the aircraft. There were no injuries, and no damage to the aircraft was reported.

C-GTVL, Bell 206-B3 helicopter, operated by Quantum Helicopters, was conducting a local animal survey flight, under visual flight rules, from Williams Lake Airport (CYWL), BC. While flying at approximately 9 300 feet above sea level (ASL) the pilot heard a loud bang and the helicopter yawed. The engine (Rolls Royce Allison 250-C20B) indications showed that the engine had lost power. Concurrently, there was smoke in the cockpit, a warning horn, and the engine chip warning illuminated. The pilot broadcast a MAYDAY call and turned on the emergency locator transmitter (ELT). The pilot executed a successful autorotation and landed in a meadow at approximately       6 800 feet ASL. Once the pilot and passengers egressed, the pilot used the satellite phone to contact the British Columbia Wildfire Service (BCWFS). The BCWFS dispatched 2 helicopters to recover the pilot and passengers and relayed to the Joint Rescue and Coordination Centre that the pilot was turning off the ELT and that further support was not required. There were no injuries, and the helicopter was not damaged.The helicopter was airlifted from the landing site, and it was determined that the engine failure may have initiated at the top mounting structure at the exhaust collector. Internal engine damage was consistent with the turbine being out of alignment and there were indications of blade rub. The engine was sent for further examination.

C-FTHD, a Summit Helicopters Limited Bell 407 departed Kamloops Airport (CYKA), BC, under visual flight rules for a local training flight with 3 crew members on board. While in a low hover practicing fire suppression using a long line and a water bucket, the trainee pilot inadvertently selected the hook release instead of water release and inadvertently dropped the bucket and long line from approximately 15-20' feet above ground level. There were no injuries; the helicopter was not damaged.

C-FLXT, an Air Spray (1967) Limited Lockheed L188C (Electra), was conducting a practice fire mission as flight ASB481, 35 nautical miles west of Williams Lake Airport (CYWL), BC. During the flight, the No.1 engine (Allison 501-D13) RPM increased to rate above operational limitations. The crew performed a precautionary shutdown of the engine as per the quick reference handbook. The aircraft returned to CYWL and landed without further incident.Company maintenance replaced propeller No.1 rotary actuator, and the aircraft was returned to service.

The Conair Group Incorporated Aero Commander 690A (registration C-GGAA) departed Abbotsford Airport (CYXX), BC, on flight FGD138 under instrument flight rules to High Level Airport (CYOJ), AB, with 2 flight crew members on board. While in cruise flight at Flight Level 230, the right engine (Garrett, TPE331-10T-516K) power and fuel flow indications began to fluctuate. The crew declared an emergency with air traffic control and initiated a descent with the intention of diverting to Kamloops Airport (CYKA), BC. Once power was reduced on the affected engine, the fluctuating engine indications stabilized. The crew consulted with maintenance and elected to return to CYXX where the flight landed with emergency services standing by. During the landing roll, after reverse thrust was commanded, the aircraft departed the runway centreline to the right, but remained on the paved surface of the runway. There were no injuries. The tire on the right main landing gear had a 7 cm tear on the inner sidewall. There was no other damage to the aircraft, which was towed from the runway to a company hangar. There were no injuries.A maintenance inspection determined that the engine fluctuations were caused by a faulty T2 temperature sensor located in the right engine inlet. The sensor was replaced, an engine ground run was conducted, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GNTG, a Buffalow Airways Ltd. Air Tractor AT-802A (Fireboss) on amphibious floats, was conducting training from Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT. The pilot reported a landing gear issue on approach and conducted a low pass to have a visual confirmation that the landing gear was down. The pilot requested aircraft rescue and firefighting to be on standby and landed without further issue.The maintenance team found that the left-hand nose gear track rods were overtightened. The track rods were adjusted in accordance with the maintenance manual and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FDTH, an Air Spray Ltd. Lockheed L-188A was conducting aerial firefighting operations as ASB498 locally from Manning Aerodrome (CFX4), AB, on Alberta wildfire #PWF037, (23 NM W of CFX4). On the second flight of the day, while on short final for the second drop, the fire reached a taller tree patch, which rapidly increased the intensity of the fire. This resulted in a rapid increase in fire activity and temperatures on the left side of the aircraft. The captain called for an increase in power. While power was being advanced, a temperature spike of 1040° F was noticed on the # 1 engine and was identified by the co-pilot. The flight crew observed the # 1 engine propeller speed drop and the captain called for an engine failure drill on the # 1 engine (Allison 501D-13). While securing the # 1 engine, the # 2 engine temperature spiked to 1040° F. The captain noticed the decreased performance, confirmed with power lever application and observed no change. The flight crew determined that the engine de-coupled and conducted the engine failure drill on the # 2 engine. Both engines were confirmed shutdown and propellers feathered. Once at a safe altitude, the emergency checks were completed, and a 2-engine landing was briefed. An emergency was declared and the aircraft returned to CFX4 where the aircraft landed without further issue.

C-GRSX, a privately registered Cessna 305A (L-19 Bird Dog) was operating on a cross-country flight from a private airstrip 15 NM E of Peace River, AB, to Red Deer Regional Airport (CYQF), AB. An en-route stop was planned at Valleyview Aerodrome (CEL5), AB. While touching down on Runway 25 at CEL5, the aircraft began to drift to the left. The pilot was unable to regain control and the aircraft departed the left edge of the runway. While the left main landing gear transitioned from the paved runway surface to the grass, the aircraft began to ground loop. Subsequently the right main landing gear collapsed, and the right wing contacted the ground and fractured as the aircraft came to rest. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was uninjured.

C-FWSI, a Boeing 737 operated by WestJet Airlines was conducting flight WJA145 from Calgary Intl., AB (CYYC) to Fort McMurray, AB (CYMM). N103RM, a Cessna T310 was conducting a night VFR forest fire mapping flight southwest of the Fort McMurray Airport, AB (CYMM). During the RNAV Y approach into CYMM, the flight crew of WJA145 was made aware of VFR traffic in the vicinity of CYMM by ATS. The pilot of N103RM was operating outside of the CYMM control zone and monitoring 126.7 MHz. However, ATS was unable to make any radio contact with N103RM on any of the designated frequencies. Approximately 11 nm SW of CYMM, WJA154 took evasive action to avoid traffic by performing a right hand race track pattern before continuing the approach for an uneventful landing in CYMM.Separation was reduced to 2.3 nm laterally and 200' vertically, when 3 nm laterally or 1000' vertically are required.

C-FPMR, a Great Slave Helicopters 2018 Ltd., Bell Textron Inc. 212 was operating in support of forest fire suppression activity near Fort Good Hope, NT. Shortly after lift off from the Fort Good Hope Airport (CYGH), NT, the helicopter experienced a separation of one main rotor blade from the head. Shortly thereafter, the remaining rotor blade and head separated from the mast. The helicopter subsequently collided with terrain. The pilot, who was the only occupant, received fatal injuries. There was a post impact fire. The TSB Edmonton office deployed 2 investigators.

C-GMFW, a Bombardier CL-215-6B11 (Series CL-415) operated by Air Spray (1967) Ltd., was conducting a VFR flight from Fire 20; located approximately 70 nautical miles NW of Thompson Airport (CYTH), MB to CYTH. C-GMFW was southeast bound at 3500 feet, monitoring and making position reports on 126.7 MHz, and monitoring the BirdDog frequency. Two accompanying aircraft, C-GMFY and C-GJFO, were flying the same route at 1500 feet ASL and ahead of C-GMFW. C-GMFY notified C-GMFW that a De Havilland DHC-2 aircraft was overhead their position at an unknown altitude. C-GMFY attempted to communicate with the DHC-2 aircraft but there was no response. C-GMFW subsequently observed the DHC-2 as it passed 90 degrees of their track and a few hundred feet off their right wing. The visibility at the time was hazy in smoke and the color of the DHC-2 was white.

C-GSUJ, an Air Spray (1967) Ltd. Rockwell 690A, was conducting forest fire fighting operations approximately 45 NM NW of the Fort McMurray Airport (CYYM), AB. About 1 hour and 45 minutes into the flight, the pilot observed low oil pressure and fluctuating power indications on the left engine (GARRETT, TPE331-10T-516K). There were no asymmetrical power affects on the aircraft and the engine temperatures remained normal. The pilot decided to return to CYMM and conducted a visual approach for Runway 26. While in the flare the aircraft yawed and rolled fairly abruptly. The pilot brought both power levers to idle and set the aircraft down on the runway. Directional control was difficult and the aircraft departed the right side of the runway and came to rest in the grass. The aircraft was shut down and the pilot and fire attack officer egressed with no issue and no injury. There were no observed damages to the aircraft.Company maintenance found that an O-ring was missing on the oil filter housing for the left engine resulting in a significant oil leak.

C-GJTZ, a Lockheed L188C operated by Air Spray (1967) Ltd., was operating as ASB492 engaged in forest fire suppression operations based out of Loon River Airport (CFS6), AB. While in flight the crew observed that the No. 3 engine had low TIT, no horsepower, low fuel flow and high propeller RPM. The flight crew consulted the QRH and shutdown the No. 3 engine (Allison/Rolls Royce 501-D13) and diverted to Red Deer Regional Airport (CYQF), AB. The flight crew advised ATS of their situation and completed an uneventful 3 engine landing into CYQF.Company maintenance will be replacing the engine and will report to the TSB their findings.

A mid-air collision occurred between a L R Helicopters Inc. Bell 212, C-FTLR, and a Namao Flying Club Cessna 172, C-GJJL. C-FTLR was en route from Fort McMurray, AB, to Rocky Mountain House, AB, at an altitude of 3500 feet ASL and on an approximate course of 200°M; only the pilot was on board. C-GJJL was conducting a proficiency training flight with one instructor and a privately licensed pilot on board. They had completed their exercises and were returning to Villeneuve Airport (CZVL), AB, and on a track of 145°M level at 3500 feet ASL.The collision occurred 13 NM northwest of CZVL. The pilot of C-FTLR set down in a farm field shortly after the collision. C-GJJL continued on to CZVL and landed with no issue. The outer portion of the leading edge of the right wing of C-GJJL had contacted the right side of C-FTLR's tail skid/stinger.

C-GVFK (serial number E2268), a Conair Group Incorporated BAE Systems (Operations) Limited Avro Series RJ85 planned to depart Kamloops Airport (CYKA), BC, on flight number FGD564 for firefighting under visual flight rules with 2 flight crew members on board. During the takeoff roll on Runway 27, the crew observed an excessive exhaust gas temperature on the number 4 engine (Avco Lycoming LF-507-1F). The pilot monitoring reduced the thrust setting on the engine, but there was no change. The crew rejected the takeoff and applied the brakes. Once the aircraft came to a stop, the crew noted that the brake temperatures had reached 750 degrees Celsius and declared an emergency with a request for aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) services as a precaution. The aircraft was shut down in the turnaround bay at the west end of the runway and the runway was temporarily closed. Once the brakes cooled sufficiently, the aircraft was towed back to the company tanker base and the runway was reopened. Maintenance replaced the fuel control assembly on the number 4 engine and completed a power verification run. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GILZ, an Airbus Helicopters AS350B2, was being operated by West Coast Helicopters on a wild fire 31 NM west of the Slave Lake Airport (CYZH), AB. While translating into forward flight, just after picking a load of water with an external bucket from a beaver pond, the pilot heard the horn and observed the red HYDR warning light with the helicopter entering a left descending turn. The pilot jettisoned the load and turned the hydraulics off. Controllability did not improve and the pilot managed to set the helicopter down into the trees such that it remained mostly upright. The cabin sustained substantial damage and the pilot's seat broke free from the floor during the impact. This allowed an easy egress and he acquired no injuries. The helicopter sustained substantial damage; there was no post-impact fire.

C-FCHE, a Bell 205A-1 helicopter being operated by Custom Helicopters Ltd., was performing water bucketing drops at a forest fire located 12 NM south of Snow Lake, MB. The aircraft had previously performed 21 water bucket drops. On the 22nd drop, while slowing to position for the target area, the water bucket released from the cargo hook. The pilot returned to base and the aircraft was inspected. The water bucket fell into an unpopulated area and has not been recovered.The operator's maintenance determined that interference between the electrical cord and the manual release on the hook caused an inadvertent release of the water bucket. The cargo hook was inspected, and no faults were found. The electrical cord was repositioned, and the aircraft continued to perform water drops on the fire with another water bucket.

C-GJQN, a Sikorsky S61N, was being operated by Canadian Helicopters Limited in support of forest firefighting activities near Conklin, AB. While working a fire 13 NM NW of Conklin (Leismer) Aerodrome (CET2), AB, the flight crew observed an intermittent "compass fail" caution light. During an approach to refill at the water source, the aircraft began to shake laterally. The approach was abandoned and the flight crew diverted to CET2. The shaking went away but then returned with no shaking in the controls. The flight elected to do a precautionary landing in a bog and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed with no issue. The flight crew were retrieved by another helicopter and returned to CET2. Maintenance personal attended the helicopter and discovered a malfunctioning gyro that was providing input into the yaw channel of the automatic flight control system. The yaw channel was disengaged and the helicopter was ferried without issue to CET2 for further troubleshooting.

C-FFHP, a Conair Group Incorporated De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Dash 8 Q400 was operating flight FGD549 under instrument flight rules from Penticton Airport (CYYF), BC, to Abbotsford Airport (CYXX), BC. While climbing through 13 000 feet above sea level, both aircraft alternating current (AC) electrical generators tripped offline after the crew activated the aircraft propeller heating systems. A Pan Pan was declared with air traffic control, and the crew performed the applicable checklist from the aircraft quick reference handbook. Power to the AC generators was subsequently restored and the aircraft landed without further incident at CYXX.A post-flight maintenance inspection discovered an electrical short within the wiring harness of the propeller heater system. The wiring was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FSCE, un appareil Cessna R182 effectuait un vol de positionnement selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de Chicoutimi/St-Honoré, Qc (CYRC) à destination de l'aéroport de Chibougamau/Chapais, Qc (CYMT) avec seulement le pilote à bord. À son altitude croisière à 4500 pieds, environ 15 minutes après le décollage, le pilote a noté une température de sortie des gaz élevée. Croyant avoir trop appauvri il a ajusté la manette de mixture pour enrichir le mélange. Peu après, une forte odeur d'essence a été décelée et le pilote a décidé de se rediriger vers l'aéroport Dolbeau-Saint-Félicien, Qc (CYDO). En descendant à 3500 pieds pour éviter un nuage, le moteur a commencé à perdre de la puissance. Le pilote a continué à enrichir le mélange, mais le moteur a continué de perdre de la puissance. Le pilote a trouvé un endroit pour se poser de force et a coupé complètement le moteur tout juste avant le toucher pour minimiser les dommages. L'appareil s'est renversé peu après avoir touché la surface molle de la tourbière. Le pilote est sorti sans blessure et a contacté les secours. L'appareil a subi des dommages importants et il n'y a pas eu d'incendie.

C-FNRP, a Rockwell Aero Commander 690C, operated by Buffalo Airways, was conducting a positioning flight as Bird Dog 104 from Inuvik Airport (CYEV), NT, to Fort Simpson Airport (CYFS), NT, with the pilot and one passenger onboard. Approximately 24 nm northeast of Norman Wells Airport (CYVQ), NT, the pilot observed smoke in the cockpit. The pilot turned off the generators and electrical system but could see and smell smoke continuing to enter the cockpit. The pilot completed the appropriate checklist, temporarily turned electrical power back on, declared PAN PAN with ATS and elected to divert to CYVQ where an uneventful landing was completed. Aircraft rescue and firefighting attended the aircraft; however, no smoke or flames were observed.Subsequent inspection by aircraft maintenance determined that the air cycle machine for the environmental/pressurization system had failed. The air cycle machine was deferred, and the aircraft continued to CYFS.

C-FCHE, a Bell Helicopter 205A-1 operated by Custom Helicopters Ltd. departed the Wekusko Fire Base, MB, on a VFR flight to perform water bucketing on a nearby fire. During the tenth water bucket run, the water bucket unintentionally released from the helicopter. The water bucket was recovered but sustained significant damage. There was no damage to property or the environment.The operator's maintenance replaced the cargo hook assembly and tested it before returning the aircraft to service.

C-GJFO, a Rockwell International Commander 690 operated by Air Spray (1967) Ltd. as flight ASB192, was conducting a local VFR flight from Thompson Airport (CYTH), MB. When the aircraft was at 2500 feet and 23 nautical miles south of CYTH, a large bird struck the left-side horizontal stabilizer. ASB192 returned to CYTH but experienced control difficulties when full flap was selected for the landing. The pilot performed an overshoot and conducted a second approach with a reduced flap setting. The aircraft landed safely. A visual inspection of the aircraft determined that the horizontal stabilizer sustained significant damage and it will be replaced.

C-FRBD, an Aero Commander Rockwell 500S aircraft operated by Mag Aerospace Canada Corp., was parked on the apron at the Dryden Regional Airport (CYHD), ON. The pilot of C-FDBD, a Commander 690A aircraft operated by Mag Aerospace Canada Corp., contacted the fueling agent and requested JET-A fuel for C-FDBD. The contracted fueling agent subsequently began fueling C-FRBD with Jet-A (the aircraft requires AVGAS). The fueling was stopped when 20 litres of JET-A was added to C-FRBD. C-FDBD was parked nearby and has similar registration markings to C-FRBD. The pilot of C-FRBD was immediately notified and the aircraft was blocked from moving by a fuel truck. C-FRBD was removed from service for fuel removal by the operator's maintenance.

C-GVCS, an Aerospatiale AS332L helicopter operated by Coldstream Helicopters Ltd., was conducting a firefighting flight approximately 35 nautical miles (NM) northwest of Kenora Airport (CYQK), ON, with 2 crew members on board. During the flight, the aircraft experienced an electrical short circuit in the DC master box (1 Alpha). This short circuit caused a number of issues in the aircraft. The aircraft was in the process of executing a water drop on the fire at approximately 250 feet radar altitude. After initial diagnosis of the problem, the crew jettisoned the bucket and long line using the manual emergency release (electrical release not usable with loss of electrical power) and then focused on recovery of altitude and airspeed. They then continued diagnosis and used the emergency range of the number 1 throttle to recover more rotor rpm. The aircraft then turned towards base. After a short period en-route, the crew decided to land the aircraft. They landed in a gravel clearing approximately 9 NM from the fire near a small settlement. There were no injuries. There was no fire. There was no damage to the helicopter.

C-FDHK, a Conair Group Inc. Air Tractor AT-802A was operating flight FGD680 on a fire suppression mission from Lac La Biche Aerodrome (CYLB), AB, to Janvier Aerodrome (CEP5), AB. The aircraft was operating as part of a 4 aircraft group conducting fire suppression activities in the vicinity of Bohn Lake approximately 2 NM east of CEP5. During a water scooping run on the lake, the aircraft experienced a porpoising event and made firm contact with the surface of the lake in a nose high attitude. The pilot brought the aircraft to a stop on the water, jettisoned the water load and then commenced a takeoff with no further issues. Another 5 scooping runs and water dumps were completed before the aircraft returned to Fort McMurray Airport (CYMM), AB, to refuel. After arrival at CYMM the pilot noticed the damage to the empennage and the missing ventral fin. The aircraft is currently undergoing repairs.

C-FYHL, a Bell 427 operated by Prairie Helicopters Inc., was conducting firefighting support operations from Rennie Fire base, MB to Whiteshell Provincial Park, MB. While conducting a toe-in hover landing in order to drop off two wildland firefighters at a rock outcropping site on the upper northwest corner of Mantario Lake, MB, the pilot heard a loud continuous noise while the aircraft was being unloaded. The helicopter then pitched nose down and the tail moved up and to the right. The pilot corrected down and to the left and the back of the skids contacted the rock surface. The pilot then rolled off the throttle, closed the two emergency fuel valves and pushed the cyclic forward and left. Once settled on the rock surface the aircraft slid backwards where it hit a rock ledge and came to rest. The aircraft was slung out of the location back to the operator's base for inspection.During inspection by the operator's maintenance, it was found that the aircraft experienced a blade strike and required a sudden stoppage inspection.

C-GUWX, a Campbell Helicopters Ltd. Bell 212 was operating on a local fire suppression mission to wildfire SWF-083, approximately 100 NM NW of the Fort McMurray Airport (CYMM), AB. The staging area for the SWF-083 wildfire was established in the vicinity of the wildfire in a muskeg area adjacent to a watercourse and swamp. After finishing a bucket cycle, the pilot proceeded to set the Bambi bucket down at the staging area to pack it up and wait for the arriving fire crew. As the pilot set the bucket down and was laying out the long-line while maneuvering to land, the pilot felt an impact from the tail and the helicopter entered an un-commanded turn. The pilot rolled both throttles to idle and the helicopter settled to the ground. The engines were shut down and the helicopter secured before the pilot exited the helicopter. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was uninjured. The helicopter received significant damage as the tail rotor had departed and struck the tail cone and right horizontal stabilizer. Examination of the Bambi bucket revealed that the tail rotor struck near the top of the bucket.

C-GRTL, an Aerospatiale AS 350 BA operated by 1000367123 Ontario Ltd. (dba Heli-Worx Aviation), was conducting fire suppression work from Savant Lake FAB (48.35 NM ENE of Sioux Lookout Airport (CYXL), ON), to SLK003 (49.94 NM NE of CYXL). While suppressing a spot fire at SLK003, the pilot unintentionally pushed the external load release and the bucket disconnected from the aircraft. The bucket was approximately 100 feet from the ground and no ground personnel were injured. There was no damage to the aircraft.

C-GSGK, a Bell 205A-1 operated by Guardian Helicopters Inc., was operating a VFR flight from Bak Lake Forward Attack Base, ON conducting aerial firefighting activities near Sandy Lake Airport, ON (CZSJ). At approximately 17:51 CDT, shortly after scooping a load of water from a lake, the engine (Avco Lycoming T5313B) stopped producing power. The pilot (sole occupant) released the water load and conducted an autorotation landing in a shallow part of the lake. The pilot was uninjured. The ELT activated and another helicopter in the area responded to the site and rescued the pilot. The operator's maintenance went on site to rig the aircraft to lift it out of the water. They discovered some metal debris in the engine exhaust and the engine couldn't be turned by hand. The helicopter was recovered and shipped back to the operator's hangar to remove the engine for a teardown. After consultation with the helicopter manufacturer, it was found that the airframe suffered extensive damage while resting in the water and during the lift operation. The TSB is awaiting the engine tear down report.

C-FGKO, an Aerospatiale AS350 B-2 operated by Custom Helicopters was conducting a VFR local flight that included firefighting duties and external load operations in vicinity of Lynn Lake, MB. C-FGKO departed the Eldon Lake Fire Base (ELFB), located near Lynn Lake/Eldon Lake Water Aerodrome (CKD3), MB. C-FGKO was returning from the fire with a 100-foot-long line and a 16-foot x 16-foot net that weighed approximately 380 pounds. The helicopter approached ELFB into wind from the south. The drop zone was on the north end of a pad area near where C-GLBJ, a Wildcat Helicopters Inc. Airbus AS 350 B3, was parked. The pilot attempted to stabilize the load but drifted closer to the parked helicopter and elected to go around. On the second approach, ground crew arrived to help marshal the helicopter. On the final approach to the drop site, the load made contact with the water, short of the dock. Engine power was increased to gain altitude and bring the helicopter into a hover; however, the load had lateral and longitudinal movement. During the attempt to regain control, the load made contact with 2 of C-GLBJ's rotor blades. The pilot released the load at a height of 2 to 3 feet above the ground. The pilot landed the helicopter safely and shut down.Wildcat Helicopters' maintenance removed the 2 blades from C-GLBJ for inspection.

C-FIGS, a Cessna 337 aircraft operated by MAG Aerospace Canada Corp. was conducting a local VFR fire patrol flight from La Ronge/Barber Field Airport (CYVC), SK. When approximately 40 NM North-northwest of CYVC, the pilot observed an RPM fluctuation on the front engine which worsened over time. The pilot then turned back toward CYVC and consulted the quick reference handbook emergency checklist (QRH). While actioning the "propeller overspeed/governor" checklist, the front engine was inadvertently shut down. The pilot restarted the front engine and was unsure of the front engine's performance. He declared a PAN PAN to receive priority through restricted airspace and the aircraft landed at 0048 UTC in CYVC without further incident.The operator's maintenance department found a broken tachometer wire on the right magneto of the front engine. The wire was repaired with a new terminal end, and a satisfactory function test carried out. The aircraft was returned to service. The operator will be amending the QRH to have the "low, high/fluctuating RPM gauge" checklist appear before the propeller "overspeed/governor failure" checklist.

C-GHVJ, un Cessna 182R exploité par Exact Air inc. effectuait une patrouille de feu selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Chibougamau/Chapais, QC (CYMT) avec seul le pilote à bord. Après environ 5 minutes de vol, une odeur inconnue est apparue dans la cabine, et quelques minutes plus tard, de la fumée a commencé à sortir autour du transpondeur. Le circuit électrique a immédiatement été fermé et un retour à CYMT a été amorcé. Ayant isolé le transpondeur, l’électricité a été rétablie pour sortir les roues et les volets, et par la même occasion déclarer un état d’urgence. L’aéronef s’est posé sur la piste 04 sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-FXDM, an Aerospatiale AS 350 FX2 operated by Airborne Energy Solutions Inc., was conducting long line firefighting operations utilizing a bucket out of a remote location approximately 48 NM south-southeast of High Level Airport (CYOJ), AB. After returning to the camp for the day, the pilot placed the water bucket on the ground behind the landing pad and was positioning the helicopter to the landing pad. During the reposition, the rotor downwash inflated the bucket, and the bucket made contact with the tail rotor. The helicopter gained approximately 15 feet of altitude and completed one revolution before contacting the ground and rolling onto its right side. Company maintenance personnel immediately responded, shut down the helicopter and extricated the pilot from the cockpit through the roof window. There were no injuries, but the helicopter was significantly damaged.

C-FNWD, a WestJet Boeing 737-8 (Max 8) departed Tampa International Airport (KTPA), FL, as flight WJA1285, under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. Shortly after arriving at the gate at CYVR, the flight crew was alerted by the ground crew to the presence of flames coming from the number one engine (CFM International LEAP 1B27). The flight crew was unable to visually verify the engine fire due to the passenger boarding bridge blocking their view. The flight crew checked the cockpit for indications of an engine fire. The cabin crew, having been made aware of the fire, initiated evacuation procedures to get the passengers off the plane after receiving confirmation from the flight crew. The flight crew gave the order to evacuate through the aircraft’s public address system and conducted the Engine Fire on Ground checklist and the Evacuation checklist. As part of the first checklist, the aircraft’s left engine halon fire suppression system was activated. Sixty-five passengers egressed the aircraft using the passenger boarding bridge while the remaining fifty-six passengers egressed the aircraft using the rear emergency slides located at the rear aircraft doors. Aircraft rescue and firefighting crews were dispatched to the scene and inspected the aircraft; however, the tail pipe flame had extinguished prior to their arrival. There were no reported injuries. There was no damage to the aircraft.Maintenance found that the center vent tube extension (CVTE) had a significant amount of oil coking which caused the oil to pool in the exhaust nozzle. The pooled oil ignited after the engines were shut down due to the heat in the exhaust cone and this created the tail pipe fire. An inspection for engine exposure to fire and extinguishing agents was carried out successfully. The CVTE, exhaust tube support, and injection nozzle were all removed and cleaned. The CVTE extension was replaced. The rear aircraft emergency slides were replaced as was the left engine halon fire bottle. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FDSN, a VIH Helicopters Ltd. Sikorsky S61N was conducting a flight in support of firefighting operations from Lac La Biche Aerodrome (CYLB), AB, to a remote site approximately 50 nm north of CYLB. Early in cruise, the flight crew observed noticeable main rotor vibration and commenced a precautionary landing. Prior to touchdown, the bucket and longline assembly were released from the helicopter to facilitate the landing. The helicopter landed uneventfully, there were no injuries.After landing, it was determined that a fault in the automatic flight control system (AFCS) was the cause of the vibration. The fault was rectified, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FWTY, a Bell 412 aircraft operated by Wildcat Helicopters, departed the Surmont Camp [Fort McMurray International Airport (CYMM), AB, 26 NM southeast] to support firefighting operations in the area. While in cruise the pilot heard a loud bang as the helicopter yawed. The pilot observed that the #2 engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PT6T-3D) failure caution light had illuminated. The pilot ran the appropriate emergency procedure and diverted to CYMM for an emergency single-engine approach landing. The landing was completed without incident.

C-FMFP, a Rockwell 690A aircraft operated by the Saskatchewan Public Safety Agency as flight BD166, was conducting a local VFR flight from the Prince Albert/Glass Field Airport (CYPA), SK. While returning to CYPA, the crew observed the "low fuel" warning. In anticipation of a fuel shortage, an emergency was declared and an engine was shutdown to conserve fuel. The aircraft landed uneventfully at CYPA with aircraft rescue and firefighting services standing by.The operator's maintenance department discovered that the fuel indicating system was reading high. The aircraft was ferried to a maintenance base and the fuel indicating system was recalibrated.

C-GCGB, an Airspan Helicopters Ltd. Bell 212, was transporting wildfire crews near Bison Lake, AB, approximately 49 nm ENE of Manning Airport (CFX4), AB. While transiting to a fire suppression area NE of Bison Lake the pilot observed a 'TRANS OIL PRESSURE' light accompanied by a drop in transmission oil pressure. The pilot reduced power and landed immediately and shut down the aircraft. The pilot and passengers disembarked the aircraft without further incident.Following the flight the maintenance team found a ruptured transmission oil line. The line was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FMFD, a privately registered Piper PA-18-150, was conducting a VFR flight near Stormer Lake, ON, to Red Lake (Howey Bay) Water Aerodrome (CKS4), ON. While enroute, the airplane was flying at approximately 500 feet above ground level and slowed to an estimated 70 miles per hour at an idle power setting, over a lodge near Stormer Lake to observe damage conditions of the area from a recent forest fire. When power was applied to regain airspeed, the inability to move the throttle from its idle position was reported. The airplane was unable to maintain altitude and struck terrain. There were no injuries, and the airplane was substantially damaged.  After the accident, a maintenance facility inspected the function of the throttle linkage and found it to move freely.

C-GJIX, an Airbus Helicopters AS 350 B-2 aircraft operated by Custom Helicopters Ltd., was conducting local external load wildfire fighting operations from Goose Bay Airport (CYYR), NL. The helicopter departed the company hangar at CYYR and crossed Runway 15/33 heading south with a slung long line and Bambi Bucket attached. The helicopter was in the departure climb below 500 feet above ground when the long line and bucket detached. The slung load fell in the CYYR airport midfield, and no persons or structures were in the area where the load fell. The minor damage to the bucket from the unintentional release was repaired. A full inspection and test of the external hook, long line and bucket was conducted with no faults found. It is considered that the external load was not adequately secured before the departure on the occurrence flight.

C-FIRS, a Forest Protection Limited Air Tractor AT8T, operating as TKR229 was enroute from Miramichi Aerodrome (CYCH), NB, to Fredericton International Airport, (CYFC), NB. Departing CYCH after reloading with water and foam for one additional suppression 9 NM north and then the occurrence aircraft with an additional 3 other Air Tractors were returning to CYFC.  The flight of 4 aircraft were enroute to CYFC when at the hallway point, the occurrence aircraft received a low fuel annunciator. At this point the pilot activated the fuel boost pump and engine igniters. The pilot informed the team lead of the situation, and it was decided TKR229 would have priority to land. While maneuvering to enter the control zone the aircraft’s engine flamed out. The pilot declared an emergency and conducted a forced approach on to a roadway 8 NM north from CYFC. On landing the aircraft struck construction signs during the rollout. The pilot was uninjured.Maintenance inspected the aircraft and noted leading edge damage to both wings, two areas of the fuselage and damage to one propeller blade. Both wing tanks were drained, and it was determined that there was approximately 25 liters in the RH wing tank and 150 liters in the LH wing tank. Maintenance removed both wings and transported the aircraft back to the base via road. The damaged area of each leading edge was then removed to facilitate inspection of the wing spar. No wing spar damage was evident.

C-FCNU, a Range Helicopters Inc. Bell 212, was operating on a local fire suppression mission to wildfire HWF 106, approximately 39 NM northwest of High Level Airport (CYOJ), AB. The helicopter was engaged in transporting firefighters from the fire back to the abandoned Zama Airport, AB (N59 09 W118 42). The helicopter landed at HWF 106 wildfire pickup location and loaded 9 firefighters onboard. During departure, 200 meters away, the No. 1 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada, PT6T-3B) experienced a complete power loss. The pilot initiated the engine out emergency procedures and turned back intending to land at the departure location. The pilot quickly realized that the intended landing site was not achievable, and a secondary landing zone was identified. The pilot executed the single-engine emergency landing without issue. The helicopter was undamaged and there were no injuries. The pilot stayed with the helicopter and the firefighters were picked up by another helicopter.

C-GZNR, an Airbus Helicopters AS350 B3e operated by the Nova Scotia Department of Natural Resources and Renewables, was conducting aerial fire suppression operations near Five Finger Lake, NS (44°40'26"N, 065°11'19"W). While refilling the water bucket from the lake and beginning to lift off with the load at approximately 75 feet above the lake surface, the pilot reported hearing a loud bang followed by a loss of power. The helicopter subsequently impacted the water and became partially submerged. The pilot sustained serious injuries and was transported to hospital for medical treatment. The TSB is investigating.
